kanz.f: What is the ruling on praying in a ship while sitting without an excuse?
kanz.b: It is valid.

kanz.f: How many missed prayers must be made up by one who faints or goes insane?
kanz.b: If it is [the duration of] five prayers or less, they make them up; if more, they do not.

kanz.f: How many verses require a prostration of recitation (Sujud al-Tilawah)?
kanz.b: Fourteen, including the first in Al-Hajj and Sad.

kanz.f: Who is required to perform Sujud al-Tilawah?
kanz.b: The one who recites (even an imam), the one who hears it (even if unintended), and a follower (though not due to the recitation of his imam).

kanz.f: If a person praying hears a recitation verse from someone else, when do they prostrate?
kanz.b: After the prayer.

kanz.f: What if someone praying prostrates during the prayer upon hearing a recitation verse from someone else?
kanz.b: They repeat the prostration (after the prayer), but the prayer itself remains valid.

kanz.f: If one hears a recitation verse from their Imam, when do they prostrate?
kanz.b: If they complete the prayer with him before prostrating, they prostrate with him; if they finish after the Imam has already prostrated, they do not.

kanz.f: Can the Sujud al-Tilawah required during a prayer be made up outside of it?
kanz.b: No, it cannot be made up outside of it.

kanz.f: If one recites a verse outside prayer and does not prostrate, then recites it again inside the prayer, how many prostrations are required?
kanz.b: One prostration suffices.

kanz.f: How is the Sujud al-Tilawah performed?
kanz.b: With the conditions of prayer, between two Takbirs, without raising hands, Tashahhud, or Salam.

kanz.f: Is it disliked to recite a surah while omitting the prostration verse?
kanz.b: Yes, it is disliked, but the reverse (reciting only the prostration verse) is not.

kanz.f: What are the conditions to begin shortening the four-rak'ah prayer?
kanz.b: Passing beyond the city's houses with the intention of a middle-paced journey of three days.

kanz.f: If a traveler completes four rak'ahs, when is it valid?
kanz.b: If they sit at the second rak'ah (for the first Tashahhud).

kanz.f: When does a traveler stop shortening their prayers?
kanz.b: When they enter their home city or intend to reside for half a month in a town or village (excluding Makkah and Mina).

kanz.f: In what scenarios does a traveler continue to shorten their prayer?
kanz.b: If they intend a stay of less than half a month, or if they intend nothing and remain for years.

kanz.f: What is the rule for an army or those besieging a city?
kanz.b: They shorten their prayers, even if they besiege a city, unless they are dwellers in tents.

kanz.f: What is the status of a traveler who follows a resident in prayer?
kanz.b: If within the prayer time, it is valid and they complete four; after the time, it is not valid.

kanz.f: How is an original homeland (watan asli) invalidated?
kanz.b: By taking another original homeland, not by travel.

kanz.f: How is a residence homeland (watan iqamah) invalidated?
kanz.b: By taking another residence homeland, by travel, or by returning to the original homeland.

kanz.f: How are missed prayers (travel vs. residence) made up?
kanz.b: Based on their status at the end of the prayer time (traveler makes them up as two; resident as four).

kanz.f: Whose intention matters for travel and residence?
kanz.b: The original person; the dependent (woman, slave, soldier) follows the intention of the one they are dependent upon.

kanz.f: How is a "city" defined for the purpose of Jumu'ah prayer?
kanz.b: Any place with a leader and a judge who enforces rulings and establishes hudud punishments.

kanz.f: When is the time for Jumu'ah prayer?
kanz.b: The same as the time for Dhuhr; it is invalidated if the time for Dhuhr expires.

kanz.f: What is the minimum number of people required for the Jumu'ah congregation?
kanz.b: Three people besides the imam.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if the congregation disperses before the imam’s prostration?
kanz.b: The Jumu'ah is invalidated.

kanz.f: What are the requirements for Jumu'ah to be obligatory upon someone?
kanz.b: Residence, being male, health, freedom, and sound eyes and legs.

kanz.f: If someone not obligated to perform Jumu'ah performs it anyway, does it count?
kanz.b: Yes, it counts as their obligatory prayer for that time.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on praying Dhuhr before Jumu'ah for one who is not excused?
kanz.b: It is disliked; if they then strive for Jumu'ah, the Dhuhr prayer is invalidated.

kanz.f: If someone catches Jumu'ah during the Tashahhud or the prostration of forgetfulness, how do they complete it?
kanz.b: They complete it as Jumu'ah.

kanz.f: What is forbidden once the imam exits for the sermon?
kanz.b: Voluntary prayer and speech.

kanz.f: When does it become obligatory to strive for Jumu'ah and refrain from buying/selling?
kanz.b: Upon the first Adhan.

kanz.f: What is the procedure for the Adhan and Iqamah during Jumu'ah?
kanz.b: The Adhan is called when the imam sits on the pulpit, and the Iqamah is called after the sermon is completed.

kanz.f: Who is the Eid prayer obligatory upon?
kanz.b: Those upon whom Jumu'ah is obligatory, with the same conditions (excluding the sermon).

kanz.f: What are the recommended acts for Eid al-Fitr?
kanz.b: Eating, performing ghusl, using the siwak, applying perfume, wearing best clothes, and paying Sadaqat al-Fitr.

kanz.f: What is the timing for the Eid prayer?
kanz.b: From the rising of the sun until its zenith.

kanz.f: How many additional Takbirs are performed in each rak'ah of Eid?
kanz.b: Three additional Takbirs in each rak'ah.

kanz.f: When are the sermons delivered for Eid?
kanz.b: Two sermons are delivered after the prayer.

kanz.f: What is the rule if the Eid prayer is missed with the Imam?
kanz.b: It is not made up.

kanz.f: What is the difference between Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha regarding eating?
kanz.b: For Fitr, one eats before the prayer; for Adha, eating is delayed until after the prayer.

kanz.f: What is the Takbir at-Tashriq, and when is it performed?
kanz.b: Saying "Allah is the Greatest" (until the end of the phrase); it is Sunnah from the Fajr of Arafah to the Asr of the last day of Tashriq.

kanz.f: Under what conditions is the Takbir at-Tashriq performed?
kanz.b: Residency, city, obligatory prayer, and congregation (though individual performance is accepted).

kanz.f: When does the Takbir at-Tashriq become obligatory?
kanz.b: When following an Imam, it becomes obligatory for the woman and the traveler.

kanz.f: How is the Solar Eclipse (Kusuf) prayer performed?
kanz.b: The Jumu'ah Imam leads two rak'ahs like a voluntary prayer, without reciting aloud or a sermon.

kanz.f: What does the Imam do after the eclipse prayer?
kanz.b: He supplicates until the sun clears.

kanz.f: What is the procedure if there is no Imam to lead the eclipse prayer?
kanz.b: They pray individually.

kanz.f: Which events follow the same ruling as the Solar Eclipse?
kanz.b: Lunar eclipses (Khusuf), darkness during the day, storms, and terror.

kanz.f: How is the Prayer for Rain (Istisqa') performed?
kanz.b: It is a prayer, but not in congregation. It consists of supplication and seeking forgiveness.

kanz.f: Does the Prayer for Rain include turning one's cloak or the attendance of a dhimmi?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: For how long do the people go out for the Prayer for Rain?
kanz.b: They go out for three days.

kanz.f: How is the Prayer of Fear (Salat al-Khawf) structured for a resident Imam leading two groups?
kanz.b: He leads the first group in two rak'ahs, they depart, then he leads the second group in the remaining two.

kanz.f: In the Prayer of Fear, how does a traveler-Imam divide the rak'ahs between two groups?
kanz.b: He leads the first group in one rak'ah, and the second group in the remaining one.

kanz.f: What is the procedure for the first group to complete their prayer in Salat al-Khawf?
kanz.b: They return, complete their rak'ahs without recitation, perform the Salam, and depart to face the enemy.

kanz.f: What is the procedure for the second group to complete their prayer?
kanz.b: They complete their remaining rak'ahs with recitation.

kanz.f: In the Prayer of Fear, how is Maghrib prayer divided between the two groups?
kanz.b: The Imam leads the first group in two rak'ahs and the second group in one rak'ah.

kanz.f: What happens to the prayer of one who begins fighting during Salat al-Khawf?
kanz.b: Their prayer is invalidated.

kanz.f: When is it permitted to pray while riding by gesturing in any direction?
kanz.b: When the fear is intense; it is not permitted without the presence of an enemy.

kanz.f: How is a dying person positioned, and what is prompted to them?
kanz.b: They are turned to face the Qiblah on their right side and prompted with the Shahada.

kanz.f: What is done immediately after a person dies?
kanz.b: Their jaw is bound, eyes closed, they are placed on a bier facing the Qiblah, and the body is covered.

kanz.f: When washing the deceased, what is the ruling on rinsing the mouth and nose?
kanz.b: They are stripped and washed without rinsing the mouth or nose.

kanz.f: What type of water and herbs are used to wash the body, head, and beard?
kanz.b: Water boiled with sidr (lotus jujube) or hurd (alkali) is poured over them; the head and beard are washed with khatmi (marshmallow).

kanz.f: What is the physical procedure for washing the sides and stomach of the deceased?
kanz.b: They are washed on the left side, then the right. They are sat up supported, the stomach is wiped gently, and any exit is washed without repeating the full washing.

kanz.f: What is applied to the deceased after drying them with a cloth?
kanz.b: Hanut (embalming mixture) is placed on the head and beard, and camphor is placed on the places of prostration.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to comb the hair or clip the nails/hair of the deceased?
kanz.b: No, hair is not combed, nor are nails or hair clipped.

kanz.f: What constitutes the Sunnah shroud for a man?
kanz.b: An izar (lower garment), a qamis (shirt), and a lifafah (wrapper).

kanz.f: What is the minimal requirement for a man's shroud?
kanz.b: An izar (lower garment) and a lifafah (wrapper).

kanz.f: What constitutes the Sunnah shroud for a woman?
kanz.b: A shift, an izar, a head-veil, a wrapper, and a cloth to bind her breasts.

kanz.f: What is the minimal requirement for a woman's shroud?
kanz.b: An izar, a wrapper, and a head-veil.

kanz.f: What is the physical sequence of putting on a woman's Sunnah shroud?
kanz.b: The shift is worn first, her hair is braided into two plaits across her chest over the shift, the head-veil goes over that, and all is placed under the wrapper.

kanz.f: How many times are the shrouds perfumed with incense?
kanz.b: An odd number of times.

kanz.f: Who has the most right to lead the funeral prayer?
kanz.b: The Sultan, followed by the judge (if present), then the local Imam, then the guardian.

kanz.f: What happens if someone other than the Sultan or guardian leads the funeral prayer?
kanz.b: The guardian repeats the prayer, and no one else prays after him.

kanz.f: If a deceased person is buried without a prayer, what should be done?
kanz.b: The prayer is performed over the grave as long as the body has not decomposed.

kanz.f: What is the breakdown of the four Takbirs in the funeral prayer?
kanz.b: 1st: Praise (Hamd). 2nd: Blessings on the Prophet ﷺ. 3rd: Supplication (Dua). 4th: Two Salams.

kanz.f: What should a follower do if the Imam says a fifth Takbir?
kanz.b: They do not follow the Imam in the fifth Takbir.

kanz.f: What is the supplication said during the funeral prayer for a child?
kanz.b: "O Allah, make him a forerunner for us, and make him a reward and a treasure for us, and make him an intercessor for us, whose intercession is granted."

kanz.f: Where should the Imam stand in relation to the deceased body?
kanz.b: One stands by the chest for both men and women.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to perform the funeral prayer while riding or inside a mosque?
kanz.b: No, it is not prayed while riding nor in a mosque.

kanz.f: What determines whether a newborn child or a captured child is prayed over?
kanz.b: Whoever cries out at birth is prayed over. A captured child is prayed over unless one parent, the child, or neither was captured with them.

kanz.f: What is the obligation of a Muslim guardian toward a deceased disbelieving relative?
kanz.b: The Muslim guardian washes, shrouds, and buries the disbeliever.

kanz.f: What is the manner and speed of carrying the bier?
kanz.b: It is taken by its four legs and carried quickly, but without running.

kanz.f: What is the sequence for an individual to carry the four corners of the bier?
kanz.b: Place the front right on your right shoulder, then the back right, then the front left, then the back left.

kanz.f: From which side is the body entered into the lahd (niche) of the grave?
kanz.b: From the Qiblah side.

kanz.f: What does the person placing the body into the grave say?
kanz.b: "In the name of Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

kanz.f: What materials should be used to level over the grave, and what should be avoided?
kanz.b: Mud bricks and reeds are leveled over it; kiln-baked bricks and wood are avoided.

kanz.f: What is the difference between a man's and a woman's grave during burial?
kanz.b: The woman's grave is covered with a screen, but not the man's.

kanz.f: How should the exterior shape of the grave be finished?
kanz.b: The earth is poured and the grave is humped; it is not squared nor plastered.

kanz.f: Who is legally classified as a martyr (shahid) regarding funeral rites?
kanz.b: One killed by those at war, rebels, or highway robbers; or one found in battle with an injury; or one killed by a Muslim wrongfully where no blood money is required.

kanz.f: What is the rule for shrouding, washing, and praying over a martyr?
kanz.b: They are shrouded and prayed over without washing, and buried in their blood and clothes.

kanz.f: Can the clothing/shroud of a martyr be adjusted?
kanz.b: Yes, items that are not part of the shroud may be added or subtracted.

kanz.f: When must a martyr be washed?
kanz.b: If they were in a state of major impurity, if they were a child, or if they were irtatha (survived for a period after the wound, e.g., ate, slept, or received treatment).

kanz.f: When else is a martyr washed despite being killed on the battlefield?
kanz.b: If they were transported from the battlefield, made a will, were killed in a city without proof of wrongful weapon-killing, or were killed by legal punishment (hadd) or retaliation (qisas).

kanz.f: Is a martyr killed by rebels or highway robbers washed?
kanz.b: No, they are not washed.

kanz.f: Is it valid to perform obligatory and voluntary prayers inside or on top of the Ka'bah?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: In what position is it valid for a follower to stand in relation to the imam inside the Ka'bah?
kanz.b: It is valid if they place their back toward the imam's back.

kanz.f: Is it valid for a follower to stand facing the imam's face inside the Ka'bah?
kanz.b: No, it is not.

kanz.f: When is it valid to form a circle around the Ka'bah for prayer?
kanz.b: It is valid for those closer to the Ka'bah than the imam, provided they are not on the same side.

kanz.f: How is Zakat legally defined?
kanz.b: It is the transfer of ownership of wealth to a poor Muslim who is neither Hashimite nor their client, on the condition that the benefit is severed from the owner in every way, for the sake of Allah Most High.

kanz.f: What are the five conditions for the obligation of Zakat?
kanz.b: Sanity, puberty, Islam, freedom, and ownership of a nisab.

kanz.f: What are the conditions for the wealth itself to be subject to Zakat?
kanz.b: It must have passed a lunar year, be free from debt and basic necessities, and be productive (even if only potentially).

kanz.f: What are the three scenarios when intention (niyyah) for Zakat is considered valid?
kanz.b: 1. Contemporaneous with the performance of giving it. 2. When setting aside what is due. 3. When giving everything in charity.

kanz.f: What is the definition of Sawa'im (grazing livestock) for Zakat?
kanz.b: Animals that suffice with grazing for most of the year.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 25 camels?
kanz.b: One bint makhad (one-year-old female camel).

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on less than 25 camels?
kanz.b: One sheep for every five camels.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 36 camels?
kanz.b: One bint labun (two-year-old female camel).

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 46 camels?
kanz.b: One hiqqah (three-year-old female camel).

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 61 camels?
kanz.b: One jadha'ah (four-year-old female camel).

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 76 camels?
kanz.b: Two bint labun.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 91 to 120 camels?
kanz.b: Two hiqqah.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 145 camels?
kanz.b: Two hiqqah and one bint makhad.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 150 camels?
kanz.b: Three hiqqah.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 175 camels?
kanz.b: Three hiqqah and one bint makhad.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 186 camels?
kanz.b: Three hiqqah and one bint labun.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 196 to 200 camels?
kanz.b: Four hiqqah.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 30 cows?
kanz.b: One tabi' (one-year-old calf) or tabi'ah.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 40 cows?
kanz.b: One musinn (two-year-old calf) or musinnah.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 60 cows?
kanz.b: Two tabi'.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 70 cows?
kanz.b: One musinnah and one tabi'.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 80 cows?
kanz.b: Two musinnah.

kanz.f: How does the obligation change for cattle counts above 80?
kanz.b: It changes every ten cows from a tabi' to a musinnah.

kanz.f: What is the ruling for buffaloes regarding Zakat?
kanz.b: They are treated like cattle.

kanz.f: What is the threshold and Zakat amount for the start of Zakat on sheep?
kanz.b: 40 sheep: one sheep.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 121 sheep?
kanz.b: Two sheep.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 201 sheep?
kanz.b: Three sheep.

kanz.f: What is the Zakat due on 400 sheep?
kanz.b: Four sheep.

kanz.f: After 400 sheep, how is the Zakat calculated?
kanz.b: For every 100 sheep: one sheep.

kanz.f: What is the ruling for goats regarding Zakat?
kanz.b: Goats are treated like sheep.

kanz.f: What age must a sheep/goat reach to be taken for Zakat?
kanz.b: It must be a thani (in its second year); a jadha (one-year-old) is not taken unless it has reached the age of a thani.

kanz.f: On which animals is there no Zakat due?
kanz.b: Horses, mules, donkeys, lambs, small camels, calves, working animals, and stall-fed animals.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on Zakat for animals that perish after the obligation has become due?
kanz.b: There is no Zakat due on them.

kanz.f: What is the definition of 'afw?
kanz.b: The amount below the nisab (minimum taxable amount).

kanz.f: If the required age of an animal is not found for Zakat, what are the options?
kanz.b: Provide a higher age and take the difference, provide a lower age and pay the difference, or provide its value.

kanz.f: What quality of animal should be selected for Zakat?
kanz.b: Average quality.

kanz.f: How is newly acquired wealth treated if it is the same type as the existing nisab?
kanz.b: It is added to the existing nisab.

kanz.f: If kharaj, ushr, or Zakat is collected by rebels, is it due again?
kanz.b: No, it is not taken again.

kanz.f: Is it valid to pay Zakat in advance for future years or amounts?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: What is the percentage of Zakat obligatory on 200 dirhams and 20 dinars?
kanz.b: One-fortieth (2.5%).

kanz.f: Is Zakat due on jewelry, raw bullion, or vessels made of gold or silver?
kanz.b: Yes, it is obligatory.

kanz.f: For gold and silver, what is the consideration for Zakat performance and obligation?
kanz.b: Weight.

kanz.f: What is the weight standard for dirhams in Zakat?
kanz.b: Ten dirhams weigh seven mithqals.

kanz.f: If an item is composed of mixed metals, how is its category determined?
kanz.b: By the prevailing material.

kanz.f: Are trade goods subject to Zakat?
kanz.b: Yes, if they reach the nisab of silver or gold.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding a decrease in the nisab during the lunar year?
kanz.b: It does not affect the obligation, provided the nisab is complete at the beginning and end of the year.

kanz.f: How are trade goods and money valued for Zakat?
kanz.b: The value of trade goods is added to money, and gold is added to silver for valuation purposes.

kanz.f: What is the role of the 'Ashir (Tithe Collector)?
kanz.b: Appointed by the Imam to collect charity from merchants.

kanz.f: In what cases is a merchant believed regarding their Zakat obligations upon taking an oath?
kanz.b: If they claim the year is incomplete, that they have debt, or that they have already paid (or paid another collector).

kanz.f: What is the exception to the rule that a merchant is believed upon oath?
kanz.b: Grazing livestock, which must be paid by the owner himself.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on claims made by a dhimmi?
kanz.b: They are believed in any claim for which a Muslim would be believed.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on claims made by a harbi (enemy alien)?
kanz.b: They are not believed, except regarding their umm walad (concubine who bore his child).

kanz.f: What are the rates collected by the 'Ashir from Muslims, dhimmis, and harbis?
kanz.b: 2.5% from Muslims, 5% from dhimmis, and 10% from harbis (provided there is a nisab and they take the same from us).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on collecting Zakat twice in one year?
kanz.b: It is not collected twice unless the year has returned.

kanz.f: Does the 'Ashir collect Zakat from wine?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: On what items does the 'Ashir NOT collect Zakat?
kanz.b: Pork, goods in one's house, merchandise, capital in mudaraba (profit-sharing), or the earnings of a permitted slave.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if rebels have already collected the tithe?
kanz.b: It is collected again by the legitimate collector.

kanz.f: What is the required share (Zakat) on Rikaz (buried treasure/minerals)?
kanz.b: One-fifth (20%).

kanz.f: On which minerals does the one-fifth requirement for Rikaz apply?
kanz.b: Gold, silver, iron, and mercury.

kanz.f: In which locations is the one-fifth requirement applicable?
kanz.b: Land subject to kharaj (land tax) or ushr (tithe).

kanz.f: Is Rikaz due on treasure found in one's own house or land?
kanz.b: No, it is not.

kanz.f: To whom does the treasure and property found in the ground belong?
kanz.b: To the one who first occupied the land.

kanz.f: Does the Rikaz ruling apply to treasure found in dar al-harb (enemy territory)?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Does the Rikaz ruling apply to turquoise, pearls, or ambergris?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: On what items is the 'Ushr (tithe) obligatory?
kanz.b: Honey from ushr land, and crops watered by rain or flowing water.

kanz.f: Are there conditions of nisab or the passing of a year for the 'Ushr?
kanz.b: No, these conditions do not apply.

kanz.f: What items are excluded from 'Ushr?
kanz.b: Firewood, reeds, and grass.

kanz.f: What is the rate for crops watered by buckets or waterwheels?
kanz.b: Half the tithe (one-twentieth, or 5%).

kanz.f: Are production costs deducted before calculating the 'Ushr?
kanz.b: No, production costs are not deducted.

kanz.f: What is the rate of tithe for land acquired by a Taghlibi?
kanz.b: Double the tithe.

kanz.f: What happens if a dhimmi buys ushr land from a Muslim?
kanz.b: Kharaj (land tax) becomes due on that land.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a Muslim acquires kharaj land from a dhimmi?
kanz.b: A tithe is due (if acquired through pre-emption or return due to sale corruption).

kanz.f: What determines the cost if a Muslim turns his house into an orchard?
kanz.b: It revolves around the water source of the orchard.

kanz.f: What is the rule for asphalt and oil springs found on ushr land versus kharaj land?
kanz.b: On ushr land, a tithe is due; on kharaj land, kharaj is due.

kanz.f: Who are the categories of people eligible to receive Zakat?
kanz.b: The poor, the destitute, the administrator, the one with a contract of manumission, the debtor, the one in the cause of Jihad, and the wayfarer.

kanz.f: Is it mandatory to distribute Zakat to all categories, or is one sufficient?
kanz.b: It may be paid to all of them or just one category.

kanz.f: Can Zakat be paid to a dhimmi?
kanz.b: No, it is not permitted.

kanz.f: What are some examples of prohibited uses of Zakat funds?
kanz.b: Building a mosque, shrouding the dead, paying a deceased person's debt, or purchasing a slave for manumission.

kanz.f: Can you pay Zakat to your own ascendants or descendants?
kanz.b: No, it is prohibited.

kanz.f: Can Zakat be paid to one's spouse?
kanz.b: No, it is prohibited.

kanz.f: Can Zakat be paid to the descendants of Hashim or their clients?
kanz.b: No, it is prohibited.

kanz.f: If you pay Zakat based on careful effort (taharri) and discover the recipient was ineligible, when is it still valid?
kanz.b: If the recipient turns out to be wealthy, a Hashimite, a client, a disbeliever, or a parent/child.

kanz.f: When is paying Zakat based on taharri NOT valid?
kanz.b: If the recipient is one's own slave or contract-slave.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on transferring Zakat to another city?
kanz.b: It is disliked, unless it is for a relative or someone in greater need.

kanz.f: Is it permitted to beg if one has enough for the day?
kanz.b: No, seeking charity when one has enough for the day is disliked, and one who has the day's sustenance should not beg.

kanz.f: Upon whom is Sadaqat al-Fitr obligatory?
kanz.b: Every free Muslim who possesses a nisab surplus to their housing, clothing, furniture, horse, weapon, and servants.

kanz.f: For whom must a person pay Sadaqat al-Fitr?
kanz.b: For oneself, one's poor child, servants for service, mudabbar, and umm walad.

kanz.f: For whom is Sadaqat al-Fitr NOT paid?
kanz.b: One's wife, adult child, contract-slave, or slaves owned by them.

kanz.f: What is the required amount for Sadaqat al-Fitr in terms of wheat, flour, parched flour, or raisins?
kanz.b: Half a sa'.

kanz.f: What is the required amount for Sadaqat al-Fitr in terms of dates or barley?
kanz.b: One sa'.

kanz.f: How many ratls is one sa' equivalent to?
kanz.b: Eight ratls.

kanz.f: When does Sadaqat al-Fitr become due?
kanz.b: At the dawn of the day of Fitr.

kanz.f: What happens if a person dies, converts to Islam, or is born after the dawn of the day of Fitr?
kanz.b: It is not obligatory for them (or in their name).

kanz.f: Is it valid to pay Sadaqat al-Fitr before or after the day of Fitr?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: How is Sawm (fasting) defined?
kanz.b: Abstention from eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse from dawn until sunset, with an intention from one who is qualified.

kanz.f: Which fasts allow an intention made from the night until before midday?
kanz.b: Ramadan (obligatory), Nadhar (specified vow), and voluntary fasts.

kanz.f: What is the rule for the intention of all other fasts?
kanz.b: They are not valid unless with a specific intention made the night before (tabyit).

kanz.f: How is the start of Ramadan determined?
kanz.b: By sighting the crescent moon or by the completion of thirty days of Sha'ban.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on fasting the Yawm ash-Shakk (Day of Doubt)?
kanz.b: One does not fast it except as a voluntary fast.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a person's testimony for the crescent moon is rejected but they saw it?
kanz.b: They must fast; if they break their fast, they must make it up.

kanz.f: What is the required testimony for the beginning of Ramadan?
kanz.b: The testimony of one just person (even a slave or woman).

kanz.f: What is the required testimony for the beginning of Eid?
kanz.b: Two free persons (or one free man and two free women), or a great gathering of people.

kanz.f: Does the difference in rising times (matali') of the moon matter for Ramadan?
kanz.b: No, it is of no consequence.

kanz.f: Does the fast break if one eats, drinks, or has intercourse forgetfully?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: Does the fast break if one experiences a wet dream or ejaculates due to looking?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: Does the fast break if one is cupped, applies kohl, or applies oil?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: Does the fast break if one kisses or if dust or a fly enters their throat?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: What happens if one eats food that was stuck between their teeth or vomits and it returns?
kanz.b: The fast is not broken.

kanz.f: What happens if one causes themselves to vomit or swallows a pebble or iron?
kanz.b: The fast is broken and they must make it up (qada').

kanz.f: When is kaffarah (expiation) required during a fast?
kanz.b: For intentional intercourse, or intentional eating/drinking (nourishment or medicine) during Ramadan.

kanz.f: Is there kaffarah for ejaculating outside of sexual intercourse or breaking a non-Ramadan fast?
kanz.b: No, there is no kaffarah.

kanz.f: What is the rule for an enema, nasal drops, or drops in the ear?
kanz.b: The fast is broken if they reach the interior.

kanz.f: What is the rule for treating a deep wound (ja'ifah or amma)?
kanz.b: The fast is broken if the medicine reaches the interior or the brain.

kanz.f: Is the fast broken by drops in the urethra?
kanz.b: No, it is not.

kanz.f: Is it disliked to taste or chew something without an excuse?
kanz.b: Yes, it is disliked.

kanz.f: Who is permitted to break the fast due to illness or travel?
kanz.b: Someone who fears an increase in illness, and a traveler (though fasting is better for the traveler if it does not harm them).

kanz.f: What is the ruling for a deceased person who died while validly excused from fasting?
kanz.b: No makeup (qada') is required; the guardian feeds someone for every day, similar to fitrah, if specified in a will.

kanz.f: Is continuity required when making up missed fasts?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a new Ramadan arrives, does one perform the current fast or make up the previous one first?
kanz.b: The current Ramadan takes precedence.

kanz.f: What is the ruling for pregnant or nursing women who fear for themselves or their child?
kanz.b: They may break the fast.

kanz.f: What is the obligation for an elderly person who is incapable of fasting?
kanz.b: They pay fidya (ransom) only.

kanz.f: What must a child or convert do if they reach puberty or accept Islam during the day?
kanz.b: They must abstain for the remainder of the day, and they do not make up the past days.

kanz.f: If a traveler intends to break their fast but then arrives home and intends to fast within the valid time, is it valid?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: In what scenarios involving "mistaken" fasting or timing must one abstain for the rest of the day and make up the day (without kaffarah)?
kanz.b: A traveler arriving home, a woman becoming pure from menstruation, eating suhur after dawn, or breaking the fast thinking the sun had set when it had not.

kanz.f: Must one make up a day if they faint or experience short-term insanity?
kanz.b: Yes, one makes up for the days missed.

kanz.f: What must one do if they vow to fast on the Day of Sacrifice (Nahr)?
kanz.b: They must break the fast and make it up (qada').

kanz.f: Under what condition does a person performing a vow to fast on the Day of Sacrifice also perform kaffarah?
kanz.b: If they intended the vow as an oath.

kanz.f: If a person vows to fast the entire year, how do they handle the forbidden days (Eids and Tashriq)?
kanz.b: They break the fast on those days and make them up later.

kanz.f: Is there a requirement for makeup (qada') if a person vows to fast, starts the fast, and then breaks it?
kanz.b: No, there is no makeup required.

kanz.f: What is the definition of I'tikaf?
kanz.b: It is the Sunnah of remaining in a mosque with fasting and an intention.

kanz.f: What is the minimum time for a voluntary I'tikaf?
kanz.b: One hour.

kanz.f: Where does a woman perform I'tikaf?
kanz.b: In her house mosque (masjid al-bayt).

kanz.f: When is a person permitted to leave their place of I'tikaf?
kanz.b: For a religious need (like Jumu'ah) or a natural need (like urination or defecation).

kanz.f: What happens if one leaves the place of I'tikaf for an hour without an excuse?
kanz.b: It is invalidated.

kanz.f: Are eating, drinking, sleeping, and trading permitted inside the mosque during I'tikaf?
kanz.b: Yes, they are permitted.

kanz.f: What is disliked during I'tikaf?
kanz.b: Bringing goods to be sold inside, remaining silent, or speaking about anything other than good.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on sexual intercourse and its preliminaries during I'tikaf?
kanz.b: They are forbidden, and intercourse invalidates the I'tikaf.

kanz.f: If one vows an I'tikaf for a specific number of days, are the nights included?
kanz.b: Yes, the nights are also required.

kanz.f: How is Hajj defined?
kanz.b: It is the visitation of a specific place at a specific time with a specific action.

kanz.f: What are the conditions that make Hajj obligatory?
kanz.b: Freedom, puberty, sanity, health, and capacity (provisions, transport, security, and a mahram/husband for women).

kanz.f: Is Hajj obligatory immediately or can it be delayed?
kanz.b: It is obligatory immediately.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a child or slave performs ihram and then attains puberty or is freed?
kanz.b: It does not suffice for their obligatory Hajj.

kanz.f: What are the Miqats (boundary points) for Hajj?
kanz.b: Dhu al-Hulayfah, Dhat 'Irq, Juhfah, Qarn, and Yalamlam.

kanz.f: Is it valid to enter ihram before reaching the Miqat?
kanz.b: Yes, but it is not valid to pass the Miqat without ihram.

kanz.f: For a resident of Makkah, what is the Miqat for Hajj and Umrah?
kanz.b: The sanctuary is for Hajj, and the hil (area outside the sanctuary) is for Umrah.

kanz.f: What is the recommended preparation for entering Ihram?
kanz.b: Perform wudu or ghusl, wear two clean garments (izar and rida), and apply perfume.

kanz.f: What is the Talbiyah?
kanz.b: "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk. Labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Inna al-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak."

kanz.f: What are the major prohibitions while in the state of Ihram?
kanz.b: Lewdness, immorality, arguing, killing/hunting game, wearing sewn clothes, covering the head/face, and applying perfume.

kanz.f: What is Idtiba' during Tawaf?
kanz.b: Wrapping the upper garment under the right arm.

kanz.f: What is Ramal?
kanz.b: Brisk walking, performed during the first three circuits of Tawaf.

kanz.f: What is Tawaf al-Qudum?
kanz.b: The arrival Tawaf, which is Sunnah for non-residents of Makkah.

kanz.f: When does one stop reciting the Talbiyah?
kanz.b: Upon throwing the first pebble at Jamrat al-'Aqabah.

kanz.f: What is Tawaf al-Ifadah?
kanz.b: The essential Tawaf (a pillar of Hajj) performed after the sacrifice.

kanz.f: What is Tawaf al-Wada'?
kanz.b: The farewell Tawaf, which is wajib (obligatory) for non-residents of Makkah.

kanz.f: What is the rule for someone who stays at Arafat but did not enter Makkah?
kanz.b: They are exempt from Tawaf al-Qudum.

kanz.f: When is the window for staying at Arafat to fulfill the Hajj requirement?
kanz.b: Between the zenith (midday) and the Fajr of the Day of Sacrifice.

kanz.f: Is the stay at Arafat valid for someone who was unconscious, asleep, or ignorant?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: Can a companion make the intention for an unconscious person?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: How does the Ihram of a woman differ from that of a man?
kanz.b: She uncovers her face (not head), does not raise her voice for Talbiyah, does not perform Ramal or run between markers, and may wear tailored clothes.

kanz.f: What is the rule for a woman’s hair during the exit from Ihram?
kanz.b: She does not shave; she only trims.

kanz.f: When does a person intending Hajj who is traveling with a sacrificial animal enter Ihram?
kanz.b: As soon as they travel with it; if they send it ahead, they enter Ihram only when they catch up with it (except for hady of Tamattu').

kanz.f: What are the three forms of Hajj, ranked from best to last?
kanz.b: Qiran (combined), then Tamattu', then Ifrad.

kanz.f: How does one declare the intention for Qiran at the Miqat?
kanz.b: "O Allah, I intend Umrah and Hajj; make them easy and accept them."

kanz.f: Does the performer of Qiran perform separate Tawafs and Sa'is for Umrah and Hajj?
kanz.b: No; they perform them for the combined pilgrimage. If they perform two of each, it is valid but sinful.

kanz.f: What is required if one performing Qiran is unable to sacrifice an animal?
kanz.b: Fasting three days (ending on the day of Arafah) and seven days upon completion.

kanz.f: When does the sacrifice become mandatory for one performing Qiran?
kanz.b: If they have not completed the fasts by the Day of Sacrifice.

kanz.f: What is the consequence of not entering Makkah and only staying at Arafat while in Qiran?
kanz.b: One owes a sacrifice for abandoning the Umrah and must make up the Umrah.

kanz.f: What are the steps for the Umrah portion of Tamattu'?
kanz.b: Enter Ihram at the Miqat, perform Tawaf, Sa'i, and shave/trim.

kanz.f: When does one cease the Talbiyah in Tamattu'?
kanz.b: At the start of the Tawaf for Umrah.

kanz.f: From where does one enter Ihram for the Hajj portion of Tamattu'?
kanz.b: From within the sanctuary (on Yawm at-Tarwiyah).

kanz.f: What happens if a person performing Tamattu' is unable to sacrifice an animal?
kanz.b: The same fasting rules apply as for Qiran (three days ending on Arafah, plus seven upon completion).

kanz.f: Does fasting three days in Shawwal before performing Umrah suffice for the Tamattu' penalty?
kanz.b: No, it does not.

kanz.f: Who is considered a Mutamatti'?
kanz.b: One who performs Umrah during the Hajj months (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah) and Hajj in the same year.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for a person in Ihram applying perfume to one limb?
kanz.b: A sheep is due (if applied to less, charity is given).

kanz.f: What is the penalty for covering the head or wearing stitched clothing for a full day?
kanz.b: A sheep is due (if for less than a full day, charity is given).

kanz.f: What is the penalty for shaving the entire head or beard?
kanz.b: A sheep is due.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for shaving a quarter of the head or beard?
kanz.b: A sheep is due.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for shaving the neck, armpits, or the area of cupping?
kanz.b: A sheep is due.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for trimming nails in one sitting?
kanz.b: A sheep is due if all hand and foot nails are trimmed; otherwise, charity is due for each of the five acts.

kanz.f: Is there a penalty for removing a broken nail?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a forbidden act (e.g., shaving/perfume) is committed due to an excuse, what are the three options for expiation?
kanz.b: Slaughtering a sheep, giving three sa' of food to six people, or fasting three days.

kanz.f: Is there a penalty for looking at a woman’s private parts with desire during Ihram?
kanz.b: No, there is no penalty, even if ejaculation occurs.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for kissing or touching with desire while in Ihram?
kanz.b: A sheep is due.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if one has intercourse before the standing at Arafat?
kanz.b: It invalidates the Hajj; one must continue the rituals, make up the Hajj later, and slaughter a sheep.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if one has intercourse after the standing at Arafat?
kanz.b: It does not invalidate the Hajj, but a camel is due as a penalty.

kanz.f: Does intercourse invalidate an Umrah if it occurs before performing most of its Tawaf?
kanz.b: Yes; one must complete the act and make it up later.

kanz.f: How is intercourse by someone who forgets treated?
kanz.b: It is treated the same as intentional intercourse.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for performing the Pillar-Tawaf while in a state of major impurity (janabah)?
kanz.b: A camel is due, and the Tawaf must be repeated.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for performing Tawaf al-Qudum or Wada' while in a state of minor impurity?
kanz.b: Charity is due.

kanz.f: What happens if one leaves most of the Pillar-Tawaf unperformed?
kanz.b: They remain in the state of Ihram.

kanz.f: How is the penalty for killing game while in Ihram determined?
kanz.b: Equivalent to the value of the animal, as determined by two just men, which is then used to buy a sacrifice, food, or for fasting.

kanz.f: Can a person in Ihram fast instead of paying for the animal killed?
kanz.b: Yes, one day for each sa' of food (the equivalent value of the animal).

kanz.f: What animals are exempt from penalties if killed while in Ihram?
kanz.b: Crows, kites, wolves, snakes, scorpions, mice, biting dogs, gnats, ants, fleas, ticks, and tortoises.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a predator attacks a person in Ihram?
kanz.b: There is no penalty for killing it in self-defense.

kanz.f: Can a person in Ihram slaughter domestic livestock?
kanz.b: Yes (e.g., sheep, cows, camels, chickens, ducks).

kanz.f: What is the status of game killed by a person in Ihram?
kanz.b: It becomes forbidden to eat, and the killer is liable for the penalty.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for a non-pilgrim killing game within the Sanctuary?
kanz.b: They pay its value in charity (no fasting is involved).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on cutting grass or trees in the Sanctuary?
kanz.b: If they were not planted by people, one must pay their value (unless dried).

kanz.f: Is it permitted to graze livestock on the Sanctuary's grass?
kanz.b: No, it is forbidden, with the exception of idhkhar.

kanz.f: What is the specific penalty for a Qarin regarding blood-sacrifices?
kanz.b: They owe two blood-sacrifices for every act that requires one from a lone pilgrim.

kanz.f: How can one invalidate the blood-sacrifice penalty for crossing the Miqat without Ihram?
kanz.b: By returning while in Ihram reciting Talbiyah, or by crossing and then entering Ihram for Umrah.

kanz.f: If a resident of Kufa enters a garden for a need, what becomes their Miqat?
kanz.b: That garden.

kanz.f: What is required if one enters Makkah without Ihram?
kanz.b: One must perform one of the rituals and then Hajj; if performed in the same year, it suffices for the unauthorized entry.

kanz.f: What is the ruling for a Meccan resident who performs one circuit of Umrah and then intends Hajj?
kanz.b: They may reject the Umrah, but they owe a Hajj, an Umrah, and a blood-sacrifice.

kanz.f: If a Meccan resident continues both Umrah and Hajj after starting the Umrah circuit, what is the consequence?
kanz.b: It is permitted, but they still owe a blood-sacrifice.

kanz.f: How does one exit Ihram if hindered by an enemy or illness?
kanz.b: By sending an animal to be slaughtered (or slaughtering it where they are).

kanz.f: How many animals does a Qarin (combined pilgrim) send if hindered?
kanz.b: Two animals.

kanz.f: Where and when does the rule of "hindrance" apply?
kanz.b: Only within the Sanctuary (Haram), and not on the Day of Sacrifice.

kanz.f: What must one do if hindered during Hajj?
kanz.b: Make up one Hajj and one Umrah.

kanz.f: Is it possible to be "hindered" after standing at Arafat?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What must someone do if they miss Hajj (by missing the standing at Arafat)?
kanz.b: Exit Ihram by performing an Umrah, and make up the Hajj the following year (with no blood-sacrifice).

kanz.f: What are the components of Umrah?
kanz.b: Tawaf and Sa'i.

kanz.f: When is performing Umrah considered disliked (makruh)?
kanz.b: On the Day of Arafat, the Day of Sacrifice, and the days of Tashriq.

kanz.f: Under what conditions is proxy performance valid for worship?
kanz.b: In financial worship (when unable to perform it oneself) and in combined worship (when incapacity is permanent until death).

kanz.f: Is proxy performance valid for purely physical acts of worship?
kanz.b: No, it is never valid.

kanz.f: Does the requirement of permanent incapacity apply to voluntary Hajj?
kanz.b: No, it applies only to obligatory Hajj.

kanz.f: Who ensures the expenses for the person performing Hajj as a proxy?
kanz.b: The person performing the Hajj on behalf of another ensures the expenses.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for the blood-sacrifice in the event of hindrance (Ihsar) during a proxy Hajj?
kanz.b: The one who ordered the Hajj.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for the sacrifice if it is for Qiran or crimes committed during a proxy Hajj?
kanz.b: The proxy.

kanz.f: If a proxy dies on the way to Hajj, how is the Hajj fulfilled?
kanz.b: It is performed from his home using one-third of his remaining wealth.

kanz.f: Is it valid to declare the intention for Hajj specifically on behalf of one's parents?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid.

kanz.f: What is the minimum requirement for a Hady?
kanz.b: A sheep.

kanz.f: What animals are permissible for Hady?
kanz.b: Camels, cows, or sheep.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on the eligibility of animals for Hady?
kanz.b: Whatever is permissible for Udhiyah is permissible for Hady.

kanz.f: Does a sheep suffice for all Hady penalties?
kanz.b: No, it suffices for all except for Pillar-Tawaf while in janabah or intercourse after the Arafat standing.

kanz.f: From which types of sacrifices is the performer permitted to eat?
kanz.b: Voluntary, Tamattu', and Qiran sacrifices.

kanz.f: When is the slaughter of Tamattu' and Qiran sacrifices restricted to?
kanz.b: The Day of Sacrifice.

kanz.f: Where must all Hady slaughtering be performed?
kanz.b: Within the Sanctuary (Haram).

kanz.f: What should be done with the coverings and rope of a Hady animal?
kanz.b: They are given away in charity.

kanz.f: Can the butcher be paid using parts of the Hady?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on milking a Hady animal?
kanz.b: It should not be milked; if necessary, the udder can be sprayed with cool water.

kanz.f: Which types of Hady are to be marked?
kanz.b: Qiran, Tamattu', and voluntary camel sacrifices.

kanz.f: What is the rule for someone who vows to perform Hajj on foot?
kanz.b: They must not ride until they complete the Pillar-Tawaf.

kanz.f: How is marriage defined in this context?
kanz.b: A contract designed to grant legal ownership of sexual pleasure.

kanz.f: What is the religious ruling on marriage?
kanz.b: It is a Sunnah; if one has intense desire, it becomes obligatory.

kanz.f: How is a marriage contract established?
kanz.b: Via offer and acceptance in the past tense, or by one of them.

kanz.f: Which specific terms are valid for establishing a marriage contract?
kanz.b: Only the words "nikah" (marriage) or "tazwij" (giving in marriage).

kanz.f: What are the requirements for witnesses in a marriage contract?
kanz.b: Two free, sane, adult, Muslim witnesses (even if they are sinners, convicted of false accusation, blind, or the sons of the parties).

kanz.f: Can a Muslim man marry a Scriptuary woman?
kanz.b: Yes, provided there are two Scriptuary witnesses.

kanz.f: What is the rule for marrying off a minor daughter if the father is present?
kanz.b: It is valid if the father orders it and it is done in the presence of a man.

kanz.f: What are the primary blood-related prohibitions for marriage?
kanz.b: Mother, daughter, sister, niece, and paternal/maternal aunt.

kanz.f: Under what condition does marriage to a step-daughter become forbidden?
kanz.b: If the mother of the step-daughter was entered into.

kanz.f: Do the marriage prohibitions apply to foster relationships?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding marrying two sisters simultaneously?
kanz.b: It is forbidden, whether by nikah or right of ownership.

kanz.f: What happens if one marries two sisters in separate contracts and cannot determine the order?
kanz.b: He must separate from both, and both are owed half their dowries.

kanz.f: What acts establish the "prohibition of affinity"?
kanz.b: Illicit intercourse, touching, or looking with desire.

kanz.f: Can a free woman marry a slave?
kanz.b: Yes, but a slave man cannot marry a free woman.

kanz.f: How many women can a free man marry?
kanz.b: Up to four (free or slave-women).

kanz.f: How many women can a slave man marry?
kanz.b: Two.

kanz.f: Why is marriage to a woman pregnant from illicit intercourse forbidden?
kanz.b: Because pregnancy from a prohibited act precludes marriage (unlike pregnancy from a lawful act).

kanz.f: What is the status of a marriage contract specified as temporary (mut'ah)?
kanz.b: It is invalid.

kanz.f: Is the marriage of an adult free woman valid without a guardian?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Can a virgin who has reached puberty be forced into marriage?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What constitutes permission from a virgin regarding marriage?
kanz.b: Remaining silent or laughing when sought by her guardian, or remaining silent after hearing of a marriage contracted by her guardian.

kanz.f: When is an explicit statement of consent required for marriage?
kanz.b: When a non-guardian seeks permission, or for a previously married woman.

kanz.f: Who is legally considered a virgin in terms of marriage guardianship?
kanz.b: One who lost her virginity through jumping, menstruation, surgery, long-term spinsterhood, or illicit intercourse.

kanz.f: Can a guardian marry off a minor (boy or girl)?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: When do minors have the right to annul a marriage contracted by a guardian?
kanz.b: Upon reaching puberty, provided a judge issues the annulment.

kanz.f: Which guardians' marriages for a minor cannot be annulled?
kanz.b: Those performed by a father or grandfather.

kanz.f: What is the order of guardianship if no asaba (male relative) exists?
kanz.b: Mother, then sister (full or paternal), then the father, then the mother’s father, then distant relatives, then the judge.

kanz.f: What is the rule if the closer guardian is at a distance of qasr?
kanz.b: A distant guardian may perform the marriage; the marriage remains valid if the closer guardian returns.

kanz.f: Who is the guardian for an insane woman?
kanz.b: Her son (not her father).

kanz.f: What can a guardian do if a woman marries someone unequal (ghayr kufu)?
kanz.b: The guardian may have the marriage annulled.

kanz.f: Does the consent of one guardian imply the consent of all?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Is silence considered consent for a guardian regarding an unequal marriage?
kanz.b: No, but receiving the dowry is considered consent.

kanz.f: What factors are considered for equality (Kafa'ah)?
kanz.b: Lineage (e.g., Quraysh/Arabs), freedom, Islam, piety, wealth, and profession.

kanz.f: What can a guardian do if the dowry is less than that of her peers?
kanz.b: The guardian may annul the marriage or require the dowry to be made equal.

kanz.f: Is it permitted for a father to marry his minor child to an unequal partner?
kanz.b: Yes, it is valid, even if there is an excessive loss (ghabn fahish).

kanz.f: Can a guardian other than a father or grandfather marry a minor to an unequal partner?
kanz.b: No, that is not permitted.

kanz.f: Can a paternal cousin marry his cousin to himself?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Can an agent marry off his client to himself?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What is the status of a marriage contract for a slave or contract-slave made without the master's permission?
kanz.b: It is suspended, treated like that of an unauthorized person (fuduli).

kanz.f: Does a marriage contract depend on the acceptance of an absent spouse?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What happens if an agent is ordered to marry a specific woman but marries two instead?
kanz.b: The marriage is invalid.

kanz.f: What happens if an agent marries a woman to a slave when ordered to marry her to a free man?
kanz.b: It is not invalid.

kanz.f: Is a marriage contract valid if no dowry is mentioned?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What is the minimum legal amount for a dowry?
kanz.b: Ten dirhams.

kanz.f: What does a woman receive if a dowry of less than ten dirhams is named?
kanz.b: She receives ten upon consummation or death.

kanz.f: How is the dowry affected by divorce before consummation?
kanz.b: It is halved.

kanz.f: If no dowry is named, what is the wife entitled to upon consummation or death?
kanz.b: The "dowry of peers" (mahr al-mithl).

kanz.f: What is a mut'ah (gift), and when is it due?
kanz.b: A gift (shift, veil, outer garment) due to a woman divorced before consummation when no dowry was named.

kanz.f: Does seclusion (khalwah) count as consummation for the purpose of the dowry?
kanz.b: Yes, regardless of impotence or castration.

kanz.f: What is shighar (exchange marriage)?
kanz.b: An exchange marriage where one gives a woman in marriage in return for the other doing the same; it requires the "dowry of peers."

kanz.f: What happens if a marriage contract includes conditions (e.g., not marrying another)?
kanz.b: If fulfilled, the promised dowry is paid; if not, the "dowry of peers" applies.

kanz.f: What is the dowry in an invalid marriage?
kanz.b: The "dowry of peers" is due upon consummation, but it cannot exceed the named amount.

kanz.f: Can a wife refuse consummation?
kanz.b: Yes, she may refuse until the dowry is paid.

kanz.f: How is the "dowry of peers" determined?
kanz.b: By looking at her father’s paternal relatives (considering factors like age, beauty, wealth, and virginity).

kanz.f: Whose permission is required for the marriage of a slave, mukatab, or umm walad?
kanz.b: The master's permission.

kanz.f: What is the consequence if a slave marries with the master's permission regarding the dowry?
kanz.b: The slave may be sold to cover the dowry.

kanz.f: Can a mukatab or mudabbar be sold to pay their dowry?
kanz.b: No, they work to earn their own dowry.

kanz.f: Does the master have an obligation to house a slave-wife?
kanz.b: No, the master is not obligated to house her.

kanz.f: Who has the right to grant permission for 'azl (coitus interruptus) regarding a slave?
kanz.b: The master.

kanz.f: What option does a slave or mukatab woman have upon being freed?
kanz.b: She has the option to choose (to stay in or exit the marriage), even if married to a free man.

kanz.f: If a slave woman marries without permission and is then freed, does she have the option to choose?
kanz.b: No, the marriage becomes valid without the option to choose.

kanz.f: What is the status of a slave woman if her master has a child with her?
kanz.b: She becomes an umm walad, and the master owes her value.

kanz.f: If a grandfather marries his son's slave woman to his son (the father), what is the status of the child?
kanz.b: The child is free, the dowry is due, but she does not become an umm walad.

kanz.f: If a non-Muslim couple marries in a way permitted by their religion, what happens if they embrace Islam?
kanz.b: Their marriage is upheld, provided the marriage was not incestuous.

kanz.f: Can an apostate (male or female) contract a marriage?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding the religion of a child born to parents of different religions?
kanz.b: The child follows the parent with the "better" religion (e.g., Islam is better than Scriptuary; Scriptuary is better than Zoroastrian).

kanz.f: What happens if one spouse converts to Islam?
kanz.b: Islam is presented to the other; if they refuse, they are separated.

kanz.f: Does a non-Muslim spouse’s refusal of Islam constitute a divorce?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Does a Muslim spouse’s refusal of the non-Muslim spouse constitute a divorce?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What effect does apostasy of either spouse have on the marriage?
kanz.b: It is an immediate annulment.

kanz.f: If a man apostatizes, what dowry is the woman entitled to?
kanz.b: If he had intercourse with her, she receives the full dowry; if not, she still receives the full dowry.

kanz.f: If a woman apostatizes, what dowry is she entitled to?
kanz.b: Nothing.

kanz.f: What happens if both spouses apostatize or convert together?
kanz.b: The marriage does not dissolve.

kanz.f: What happens if both spouses convert to Islam sequentially?
kanz.b: The marriage dissolves.

kanz.f: Is there a difference in Qasm (apportionment of time) between a virgin and a previously married woman?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Does the religious status of the wife (Muslim vs. Scriptuary) affect her entitlement to Qasm?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the ratio of Qasm between a free woman and a slave woman?
kanz.b: A free woman is entitled to double the time of a slave woman.

kanz.f: How should a man decide which wife to take with him on a journey?
kanz.b: He may choose any, but drawing lots is more beloved.

kanz.f: Can a wife waive her turn and give it to another co-wife?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: How is nursing (Rada') defined in this context?
kanz.b: An infant sucking milk from a human female breast at a specific time.

kanz.f: Within what timeframe does nursing create a marriage prohibition?
kanz.b: Within 30 months.

kanz.f: Does the amount of milk consumed affect the prohibition?
kanz.b: No, even small amounts render marriage forbidden.

kanz.f: Does milk mixed with food cause prohibition?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the rule for milk mixed with water, medicine, or milk from another source?
kanz.b: The majority (predominance) determines the effect.

kanz.f: Does milk from a virgin or a deceased woman cause the prohibition?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Does milk from a man or an animal cause the prohibition?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the consequence if a man nurses from his co-wife?
kanz.b: Both the co-wife and the nursing wife are forbidden to him.

kanz.f: How is the nursing relationship proven?
kanz.b: By the same evidence that proves property.

kanz.f: Can one marry the sister of his brother through nursing or blood?
kanz.b: Yes, this is an exception to the general rules of prohibition.

kanz.f: What is defined as the "best form" of divorce?
kanz.b: One divorce in a period of purity (tuhr) without intercourse, waiting for the ‘iddah to finish.

kanz.f: What is the "good" (Sunni) form of divorce?
kanz.b: Three divorces spread over three separate periods of purity.

kanz.f: What is the "heretical" (bid'i) form of divorce?
kanz.b: Three divorces given in one period of purity or in a single utterance.

kanz.f: Can a woman who has not been had intercourse with be divorced at any time?
kanz.b: Yes, even if she is menstruating.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on divorcing a wife during her menstruation?
kanz.b: It is bid'i; the husband should take her back and divorce her during a period of purity.

kanz.f: Does the divorce of a coerced or intoxicated husband count?
kanz.b: Yes, every sane, adult husband's divorce counts.

kanz.f: Does the divorce of a sleeping person or a child count?
kanz.b: No, it does not count.

kanz.f: How many divorces are allowed for a free woman?
kanz.b: Three.

kanz.f: How many divorces are allowed for a slave woman?
kanz.b: Two.

kanz.f: What are examples of phrases that constitute "Explicit Divorce"?
kanz.b: "You are divorced," "You are a divorcee," or "I divorce you."

kanz.f: What is the legal effect of an explicit divorce phrase, regardless of intention?
kanz.b: It constitutes one revocable divorce.

kanz.f: Does the phrase "You are the divorce" count as one or three?
kanz.b: It counts as one revocable divorce, unless he specifically intended three.

kanz.f: If a man divorces a part of the wife’s body, does it count?
kanz.b: It counts if it refers to parts representing the soul/body (neck, spirit, face); it does not count if it refers to parts like hand or foot.

kanz.f: How many divorces occur if a man says "half of a divorce"?
kanz.b: One (fractional divisions of divorce count as one).

kanz.f: What is the count if a man pronounces "three halves" of a divorce?
kanz.b: Two.

kanz.f: What is the count if a man pronounces "one-to-two" of a divorce?
kanz.b: One.

kanz.f: When does the phrase "You are divorced tomorrow" take effect?
kanz.b: At dawn.

kanz.f: What is the status of the phrase "You are divorced before I marry you"?
kanz.b: It is void.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if he says "You are divorced yesterday" and they were married today?
kanz.b: It is void.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if he says "You are divorced yesterday" and they were married before yesterday?
kanz.b: It occurs immediately (now).

kanz.f: When does "You are divorced as long as I do not divorce you" trigger?
kanz.b: It triggers upon silence.

kanz.f: When does the phrase "If I do not divorce you" trigger?
kanz.b: It does not trigger until one (the husband or wife) dies.

kanz.f: If a husband gestures with three fingers saying "You are divorced as much as this," how many divorces occur?
kanz.b: Three.

kanz.f: What is the legal effect of phrases like "irrevocably divorced" or "harsh divorce" without a specified number?
kanz.b: It counts as one irrevocable divorce, unless he intended three.

kanz.f: If a woman who has not been had intercourse with is divorced three times (in one utterance), what happens?
kanz.b: All three take effect.

kanz.f: What happens if a woman who has not been had intercourse with is divorced three times separated in time?
kanz.b: She becomes irrevocably divorced by the first one.

kanz.f: What is the result of the utterance, "You are divorced once and once" to a woman who has not been had intercourse with?
kanz.b: Only one divorce occurs.

kanz.f: What happens if a conditional divorce ("If you enter the house...") is pronounced to a woman who has not been had intercourse with?
kanz.b: Two divorces occur.

kanz.f: Do ambiguous expressions (Kinayat) automatically cause divorce?
kanz.b: No, only if intended or indicated by the state of affairs.

kanz.f: Which phrases result in a single revocable divorce?
kanz.b: "Observe your 'iddah," "Seek purity for your womb," or "You are one."

kanz.f: What is the legal effect of phrases like "You are ba'in (separated)," "severed," or "go join your family"?
kanz.b: An irrevocable divorce (ba'in).

kanz.f: If a man says "Observe 'iddah three times" without specifying intention, how many divorces occur?
kanz.b: Three.

kanz.f: Do "You are not a wife to me" or "I am not a husband to you" result in divorce?
kanz.b: Yes, if intended.

kanz.f: Can an irrevocable divorce follow another irrevocable divorce?
kanz.b: No, unless it is conditional.

kanz.f: Can an explicit divorce (Sarih) follow an irrevocable divorce?
kanz.b: Yes, explicit divorce follows both explicit and irrevocable divorce.

kanz.f: What is the result if a husband says "Choose" (intending divorce) and she chooses in the same session?
kanz.b: One irrevocable divorce.

kanz.f: When does the delegation of choice become void?
kanz.b: If she stands up or begins another task.

kanz.f: What is a condition for the validity of the delegation "Choose"?
kanz.b: Mentioning the self or "the choice."

kanz.f: What happens if he says "Choose" three times and she chooses one?
kanz.b: It counts as three divorces.

kanz.f: What is the result if the wife says "I choose myself" following a delegation?
kanz.b: She becomes irrevocably divorced by one.

kanz.f: What is the result if he says, "Your affair is in your hands for one divorce"?
kanz.b: She becomes revocably divorced.

kanz.f: If a husband says "Your affair is in your hands" intending three, how many occur if she chooses one?
kanz.b: Three.

kanz.f: In the delegation "Your affair is in your hands," how is the session defined?
kanz.b: It is restricted to the duration of the conversation; it is voided if she departs or engages in contrary actions.

kanz.f: What is the status of a divorce triggered by "Divorce yourself" (when ordered by the husband)?
kanz.b: It is a revocable divorce.

kanz.f: If he says "Divorce yourself three times" and she divorces herself once, how many occur?
kanz.b: One.

kanz.f: What is the rule for "Divorce yourself three times if you wish"?
kanz.b: If she divorces herself once, it is valid.

kanz.f: When does "You are divorced if you wish" trigger?
kanz.b: It triggers if she says "I wish."

kanz.f: What is the rule for "whenever you wish" regarding three divorces?
kanz.b: She may divide the three divorces, but she cannot combine them.

kanz.f: How must "wherever you wish" or "where you wish" be executed?
kanz.b: She is required to wish within the session.

kanz.f: Is conditional divorce valid if said to a stranger before marriage?
kanz.b: No, it is void, even if he later marries her.

kanz.f: What does the term "whenever" imply in a conditional divorce oath?
kanz.b: It implies a generalization of actions (i.e., every time the condition is met).

kanz.f: Does the termination of ownership invalidate a conditional oath?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the rule for inheritance if a husband divorces his wife during terminal illness (marad al-mawt) and dies within her ‘iddah?
kanz.b: She inherits from him.

kanz.f: What happens to inheritance if the wife requested the divorce or chose herself via delegation?
kanz.b: She does not inherit.

kanz.f: Does the wife inherit if she is divorced irrevocably during illness and the husband recovers but later dies?
kanz.b: No, she does not inherit.

kanz.f: If a man is about to be executed/stoned and divorces his wife, does she inherit if he dies?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What is Raj'ah (Revocation)?
kanz.b: The continuation of the marriage bond while the wife is still in her ‘iddah.

kanz.f: Is the wife's consent required for a valid revocation?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What verbal phrases can effect a revocation?
kanz.b: "I have taken you back" or "I have taken back my wife."

kanz.f: Can physical acts constitute a revocation?
kanz.b: Yes, acts implying marital rights such as kissing or touching with desire.

kanz.f: If a husband claims he revoked the marriage after the ‘iddah has passed, whose word is accepted if the wife denies it?
kanz.b: Her word is accepted.

kanz.f: When is revocation terminated for a woman whose ‘iddah ends after a normal menstruation cycle?
kanz.b: After ten days, even if she has not performed ghusl.

kanz.f: When is revocation terminated for a woman whose ‘iddah ends in a shorter period?
kanz.b: When she performs ghusl, or the time for a prayer passes, or she performs tayammum and prays.

kanz.f: Can a man remarry a woman he has irrevocably divorced?
kanz.b: Yes, either during or after her ‘iddah.

kanz.f: What is the condition for a man to remarry a woman divorced three times (or twice for a slave)?
kanz.b: She must marry another man through a valid contract, he must consummate the marriage, and she must complete her ‘iddah after his death or divorce.

kanz.f: Does concubinage (ownership) suffice for tahlil?
kanz.b: No, it is not sufficient.

kanz.f: What is Ila'?
kanz.b: A sworn oath to abstain from sexual relations with one's wife for four months or more.

kanz.f: What happens if a husband who has sworn an Ila' oath has relations with his wife during the timeframe?
kanz.b: He performs expiation and the Ila' is void.

kanz.f: What is the legal consequence if he does not have relations during the Ila' timeframe?
kanz.b: An irrevocable divorce occurs.

kanz.f: What happens if he swears an Ila' oath for exactly four months?
kanz.b: The oath expires (after four months).

kanz.f: What is Khul'?
kanz.b: A separation from marriage in exchange for compensation.

kanz.f: What is the legal status of the divorce resulting from Khul'?
kanz.b: It is an irrevocable divorce.

kanz.f: Is the compensation binding on the wife?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: When is it disliked for the husband to take compensation in a Khul'?
kanz.b: If he is the one at fault (rebellious).

kanz.f: What items are valid as compensation for Khul'?
kanz.b: Anything that is valid as a dowry (mahr).

kanz.f: What is the ruling if Khul' is agreed upon for forbidden goods (e.g., wine, pig)?
kanz.b: The divorce is irrevocable, but the compensation is void (she pays nothing).

kanz.f: What is defined as Zihar?
kanz.b: Comparing one's wife to a woman permanently forbidden to him (such as one's mother).

kanz.f: What is the consequence of Zihar regarding sexual relations?
kanz.b: Sexual relations are forbidden until expiation (kaffarah) is performed.

kanz.f: What is required if a man has relations before performing expiation?
kanz.b: He must seek forgiveness from Allah.

kanz.f: What constitutes "the return" (‘awd) in the context of Zihar?
kanz.b: The intent to resume sexual relations with the wife.

kanz.f: What is the hierarchy of expiation for Zihar?
kanz.b: 1. Freeing a slave; 2. If unable, fasting two consecutive months; 3. If unable, feeding sixty poor people.

kanz.f: What are the requirements for the slave to be freed as expiation?
kanz.b: The slave must be a sound believer (not blind, insane, or missing limbs).

kanz.f: What is the standard for the "feeding sixty poor people" expiation?
kanz.b: It must be equivalent to the amount of fitr charity.

kanz.f: What is Li'an?
kanz.b: Solemn oaths combined with curses, used as a substitute for the hadd punishment for qadhf (accusing the wife of adultery) or adultery.

kanz.f: In what two scenarios does Li'an become mandatory?
kanz.b: When a husband accuses his wife of adultery (and she is chaste) or when he denies the paternity of a child.

kanz.f: What is the consequence if a husband refuses to perform Li'an?
kanz.b: He is imprisoned until he performs it or retracts his statement.

kanz.f: What happens if the wife refuses to perform Li'an?
kanz.b: She is imprisoned until she performs it or confirms his accusation.

kanz.f: What is the legal outcome if both parties perform Li'an?
kanz.b: The judge separates them, resulting in an irrevocable divorce.

kanz.f: What is the effect of Li'an on the lineage of a child if the husband denied paternity?
kanz.b: The lineage is negated from the husband and attributed to the mother.

kanz.f: Can a husband remarry his wife after Li'an if he later retracts his accusation?
kanz.b: Yes, but he must first be punished for qadhf.

kanz.f: Does Li'an apply to a mute person or a denial of pregnancy?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: How is an ‘annin defined?
kanz.b: A man who cannot have sexual relations with women, or who can only have relations with previously married women but not virgins.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if a woman finds her husband has been castrated (majbub)?
kanz.b: The marriage is dissolved immediately.

kanz.f: What grace period is granted to a husband who is an ‘annin or a eunuch?
kanz.b: A one-year grace period.

kanz.f: What happens if the ‘annin husband has relations within the grace period?
kanz.b: The marriage stands.

kanz.f: What happens if the ‘annin husband fails to have relations within the grace period?
kanz.b: The judge dissolves the marriage at the wife’s request.

kanz.f: If the wife is a virgin and the husband claims he has had relations but she denies it, what is the ruling?
kanz.b: The wife is given the choice.

kanz.f: If the wife is previously married and the husband claims he has had relations, whose word is accepted?
kanz.b: His word is accepted upon his oath.

kanz.f: What is defined as ‘Iddah?
kanz.b: The mandatory waiting period for a woman following the dissolution of a confirmed marriage through intercourse or death.

kanz.f: What is the ‘iddah for a free woman after divorce or annulment?
kanz.b: Three menstrual cycles (quru') or three months if she does not menstruate.

kanz.f: What is the ‘iddah for a free woman after the death of her husband?
kanz.b: Four months and ten days.

kanz.f: How does the ‘iddah of a slave woman differ from that of a free woman?
kanz.b: It is half the duration of a free woman's ‘iddah.

kanz.f: What is the ‘iddah for a pregnant woman?
kanz.b: It lasts until she delivers.

kanz.f: What is the ‘iddah for the wife of a man fleeing to avoid inheritance?
kanz.b: It is the longer of the two periods (the normal ‘iddah vs. the ‘iddah of death).

kanz.f: What is Ihdad (Mourning)?
kanz.b: Avoiding adornments (perfume, kohl, dyed clothes, etc.) for a free Muslim woman whose marriage was irrevocably terminated or whose husband died.

kanz.f: What are the movement restrictions for a woman in ‘iddah?
kanz.b: A woman in ‘iddah for divorce cannot leave her home, while a widow may leave during the day and part of the night.

kanz.f: What is the minimum pregnancy duration for the establishment of lineage?
kanz.b: Six months.

kanz.f: What is the maximum pregnancy duration for the establishment of lineage?
kanz.b: Two years.

kanz.f: Is the lineage of a child born to a woman in a revocable ‘iddah established as the husband's?
kanz.b: Yes, even if born after two years, provided she has not confirmed the end of her ‘iddah.

kanz.f: What is the result if a man says to his slave, "If there is a child in your womb, it is mine," and a woman testifies to the birth?
kanz.b: She becomes the umm al-walad (mother of his child).

kanz.f: What is the inheritance ruling if a man claims a boy is his son and dies, and the mother claims she was his wife?
kanz.b: Both the boy and the mother inherit from him.

kanz.f: Who is most entitled to the custody of the child after separation?
kanz.b: The mother.

kanz.f: What is the order of custody if the mother is unavailable?
kanz.b: Maternal grandmother, paternal grandmother, full sister, maternal sister, paternal sister, maternal aunts, then paternal aunts.

kanz.f: Under what condition is a mother's right to custody forfeited?
kanz.b: If she marries a man who is not a mahram to the child (rights return if she separates from him).

kanz.f: If the female relatives are unavailable, who has the right to custody?
kanz.b: The ‘asaba (male paternal relatives) in the order of inheritance.

kanz.f: Until what age are the mother and grandmother entitled to custody of a boy?
kanz.b: Until he is independent, estimated at seven years.

kanz.f: Until what age are the mother and grandmother entitled to custody of a girl?
kanz.b: Until she reaches puberty.

kanz.f: Do slave women have custody rights?
kanz.b: No, unless they are freed.

kanz.f: Can a non-Muslim mother have custody of her Muslim child?
kanz.b: Yes, unless the child reaches an age of understanding the religion.

kanz.f: Does the child have a choice regarding who they live with?
kanz.b: No, the child has no choice in this matter.

kanz.f: What are the travel restrictions for a divorced mother regarding the child?
kanz.b: She may not travel with the child unless it is to her home town and she was married there.

kanz.f: What items are mandatory for a husband to provide for his wife?
kanz.b: Maintenance (food/living expenses) and clothing according to their status.

kanz.f: In which scenarios is a wife's right to maintenance forfeited?
kanz.b: If she is nashiz (rebellious), a minor unable to have relations, imprisoned for debt, stolen, performing Hajj without him, or sick before moving to the home.

kanz.f: Is maintenance for a servant mandatory for the husband?
kanz.b: Yes, if the husband is wealthy.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a husband is too poor to provide maintenance?
kanz.b: The marriage is not dissolved; the wife is instructed to borrow on his credit.

kanz.f: What is the status of past/unpaid maintenance?
kanz.b: It is not due unless it was previously ordered by a judge or agreed upon.

kanz.f: What happens to ordered maintenance if one spouse dies?
kanz.b: It is dropped (terminated).

kanz.f: What is the requirement regarding housing?
kanz.b: A separate house, free from the husband's or wife's family.

kanz.f: From where can maintenance for the family of an absent husband be taken?
kanz.b: From his assets, provided the holder acknowledges both the assets and the marriage, and a guarantor is present.

kanz.f: Is a mother required to nurse her child?
kanz.b: No, she cannot be forced to; a wet nurse is hired at the father's expense.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for the maintenance of poor parents and grandparents?
kanz.b: It is mandatory for the child/grandchild to provide it.

kanz.f: What is Manumission (‘Itq)?
kanz.b: The granting of legal capacity/freedom to a slave.

kanz.f: Who has the legal authority to grant manumission?
kanz.b: A free, competent adult toward their slave.

kanz.f: What are examples of explicit expressions for manumission?
kanz.b: "You are free," "emancipated," "liberated," or "I have freed you."

kanz.f: Besides explicit statements, how else can manumission be validly declared?
kanz.b: By a master declaring the slave as their child, father, mother, or master.

kanz.f: What is the status of a fetus if a pregnant slave is freed?
kanz.b: Both she and the fetus are freed.

kanz.f: Does a child follow the status of the mother or father regarding servitude?
kanz.b: A child follows the mother's status (ownership, freedom, or servitude).

kanz.f: What is the status of a child born to a slave-woman by her master?
kanz.b: The child is free.

kanz.f: What is the status of a slave if only part of them is freed?
kanz.b: They do not become fully free but must work for their own freedom (sa'i).

kanz.f: If a partner in a jointly owned slave frees their share, what are the other partner's options?
kanz.b: They may either free their own share or force the slave to work for their freedom.

kanz.f: What is required if a wealthy partner frees their share of a jointly owned slave?
kanz.b: They must compensate the other partner for their share in the slave's value.

kanz.f: If a master says to two slaves, "One of you is free," and dies without clarifying, what is the result?
kanz.b: Three-quarters of the first slave and half of the second are freed.

kanz.f: Which actions act as a clarification for ambiguous manumission?
kanz.b: Selling, dying, freeing, or manumitting as tadbir.

kanz.f: Does intercourse clarify an ambiguous manumission?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a man says, "If I enter this house, every slave I own at that time is free," to which slaves does this apply?
kanz.b: It applies to the slaves owned at the moment of entry.

kanz.f: If the phrase "at that time" is omitted, to which slaves does the oath apply?
kanz.b: It applies only to those owned at the time the oath was made.

kanz.f: Do "slaves" in this context include the unborn?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a man says, "Every slave I own or will own is free after two days," to which slaves does this apply?
kanz.b: It applies only to those he owned when he swore the oath.

kanz.f: If a man says, "Every slave I own or will own is free after my death," what happens to slaves acquired after the oath?
kanz.b: They are freed from his estate (up to the limit of one-third).

kanz.f: What is the status of a slave if freed in exchange for money and it is accepted?
kanz.b: The slave is free immediately.

kanz.f: What is the status of a slave if the master conditions freedom on payment?
kanz.b: The slave becomes an agent (ma'dhun).

kanz.f: When does manumission occur in a conditional payment arrangement?
kanz.b: Upon delivery of the payment.

kanz.f: If a master says, "You are free after my death for 1,000 [dirhams]," when is acceptance required?
kanz.b: After the master's death.

kanz.f: If a slave is freed for one year of service, when does the freedom take effect?
kanz.b: Upon acceptance.

kanz.f: If a slave is freed for service but dies before completing it, what is the master owed?
kanz.b: The value of the service.

kanz.f: What is Tadbir?
kanz.b: Conditioning a slave's freedom on the master's death (e.g., "If I die, you are free").

kanz.f: Can a mudabbar (slave subject to tadbir) be sold or gifted?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Is a mudabbar allowed to be used for service or hired out?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Does the status of tadbir prevent marriage or intercourse with the slave?
kanz.b: No, both are permitted.
