kanz.f: From what portion of the estate is the mudabbar freed upon the master's death?
kanz.b: One-third of the estate.

kanz.f: What happens if the master is poor and the slave's value exceeds one-third of the estate?
kanz.b: The slave must work for the value of the remaining two-thirds.

kanz.f: What happens if the master dies in debt?
kanz.b: The slave is sold to cover the master's debts.

kanz.f: What is an Umm al-Walad?
kanz.b: A slave woman who has borne a child from her master.

kanz.f: What protections does an Umm al-Walad have regarding her status?
kanz.b: She cannot be sold, and her status is protected.

kanz.f: When is an Umm al-Walad freed?
kanz.b: Upon her master’s death.

kanz.f: From what portion of the estate is an Umm al-Walad freed?
kanz.b: From his entire estate (without needing to work for creditors).

kanz.f: What is the status of the child born to an Umm al-Walad?
kanz.b: The child's lineage is established immediately.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if an Umm al-Walad was a polytheist who converted?
kanz.b: She must work for her value.

kanz.f: If a man claims a child born to a slave he shares with a partner, what is his responsibility?
kanz.b: The child is his, and he owes his partner half the child's value.

kanz.f: How is an oath (yamin) defined?
kanz.b: The strengthening of a claim by invoking a divine name.

kanz.f: What is a "plunging oath" (ghamus) and what is its status?
kanz.b: A deliberate lie about the past; it is a major sin.

kanz.f: What is a laghw (unintentional) oath?
kanz.b: An oath made out of mistaken belief about the past; there is no sin.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on oaths regarding the future?
kanz.b: They are binding and require expiation if broken.

kanz.f: Which types of expressions are valid for a formal religious oath?
kanz.b: Names of Allah (e.g., The Merciful), "By Allah," "By the covenant of Allah," or "Upon me is a vow to Allah."

kanz.f: Do oaths using non-divine entities (e.g., the Prophet ﷺ, the Quran, the Kaaba) count as formal oaths?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the expiation for breaking a binding oath?
kanz.b: Freeing a slave, feeding ten poor people, or clothing them; if unable to do these, fast for three consecutive days.

kanz.f: When is expiation required for an oath?
kanz.b: Only after the oath is broken.

kanz.f: Does an oath not to enter a "house" include the Kaaba, a mosque, or a church?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Does entering a ruin count as entering a "house" in an oath?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: If a man swears not to enter "this house" and it is destroyed and rebuilt, does the oath apply to the new structure?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a house is repaired, does an existing oath not to enter "this house" still apply?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: When is an oath "not to exit" considered broken if the person is carried out?
kanz.b: If they are carried out by their own order.

kanz.f: If one swears not to exit "except to a funeral," how can the oath be broken?
kanz.b: By staying to conduct other business after the funeral is complete.

kanz.f: If one swears to come to a person but dies before doing so, when is the oath broken?
kanz.b: At the end of their life.

kanz.f: When the phrase "if able" is added to an oath, what does "ability" refer to?
kanz.b: The physical ability associated with health.

kanz.f: If one swears not to eat busr (unripe dates) and eats rutab (fresh dates), is the oath broken?
kanz.b: No, the oath is not broken.

kanz.f: In the context of oaths, what is included in the definition of "meat"?
kanz.b: Fish, pork, human flesh, liver, and tripe.

kanz.f: What does "fat" specifically refer to in an oath?
kanz.b: Back fat.

kanz.f: How is "bread" defined for the purpose of an oath?
kanz.b: Defined by local custom (‘urf).

kanz.f: What fruits are considered "fruit" in oaths, and which are excluded?
kanz.b: Included: apples, watermelons, apricots. Excluded: grapes, pomegranates, cucumbers.

kanz.f: What is considered a "side-dish" (idam) in an oath, and what is excluded?
kanz.b: Included: vinegar, salt, or oil. Excluded: meat, eggs, and cheese.

kanz.f: What is the time frame for a Ghada' (lunch) meal?
kanz.b: From dawn until midday.

kanz.f: What is the time frame for an ‘Asha’ (dinner) meal?
kanz.b: From midday until midnight.

kanz.f: What is the time frame for a Sahur (pre-dawn meal)?
kanz.b: From midnight until dawn.

kanz.f: If one swears not to drink water from a jug today and the jug is empty, is the oath broken?
kanz.b: No, the oath is not broken.

kanz.f: If one swears not to drink water from a jug and the water is poured out, is the oath broken?
kanz.b: Yes, the oath is broken.

kanz.f: What is the status of an oath involving an "impossible act" (e.g., turning stone to gold)?
kanz.b: The oath is broken immediately.

kanz.f: How is the duration calculated for an oath "not to speak to someone for a month"?
kanz.b: It starts from the moment the oath is sworn.

kanz.f: If a person breaks a "do not speak" oath by speaking, what happens to the oath?
kanz.b: The oath becomes void.

kanz.f: Does reciting the Quran or tasbih count as "speaking" in an oath not to speak to someone?
kanz.b: No, these are not considered "speaking" in this context.

kanz.f: If a man swears, "If you give birth, you are divorced," and she gives birth to a stillborn child, is the oath broken?
kanz.b: Yes, the oath is broken.

kanz.f: In an oath regarding birth, does a stillborn child trigger manumission?
kanz.b: No, only a live child triggers it (if there is a stillborn child first followed by a live one).

kanz.f: If one swears, "Every slave I own is free," which categories of slaves are included?
kanz.b: Permanent slaves, umm al-walad, and mudabbar slaves.

kanz.f: If one swears, "Every slave I own is free," are mukattab (contracted) slaves included?
kanz.b: No, they are excluded.

kanz.f: What is the distinction between oaths regarding direct acts vs. commands?
kanz.b: Some are broken only by direct action (buying, selling, renting), while others are broken by both direct action and commanding someone else to do it (marriage, divorce, manumission, charity).

kanz.f: If one vows to walk to the Kaaba, what is required if they choose to ride instead?
kanz.b: They must offer a sacrifice (damm).

kanz.f: When is an oath "not to fast" considered broken?
kanz.b: By fasting for even a moment with the intention.

kanz.f: When is an oath "not to pray" considered broken?
kanz.b: By performing a single rak'ah.

kanz.f: Does an oath "not to sit on the ground" include sitting on a rug or mat?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Does placing a mattress on top of a specified mattress break an oath "not to sleep" on it?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Does placing a carpet or mat on top of a mattress or bed break an oath "not to sleep" on it?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Are oaths contingent on actions like striking or speaking valid if the person sworn at dies?
kanz.b: No, these oaths are contingent upon the life of the person sworn at.

kanz.f: What happens if one swears "If I do not kill so-and-so" when the person is already dead?
kanz.b: If the swearer knew of the death, the oath triggers; if they did not know, it is void.

kanz.f: Does paying a debt with counterfeit or debased coins fulfill an oath to pay?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Does paying a debt with lead or imitation coins fulfill an oath to pay?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the duration of an oath swearing not to do something?
kanz.b: It is a permanent prohibition.

kanz.f: How many times must one perform an act to fulfill an oath to do something?
kanz.b: Once.

kanz.f: If a fuduli (unauthorized person) marries someone off, when does it break the oath not to marry?
kanz.b: Only if the person accepts verbally; accepting by action does not break the oath.

kanz.f: Does an oath "I have no money" break if one is owed money by someone else?
kanz.b: No, even if the debtor is insolvent.

kanz.f: What is a Hadd?
kanz.b: A punishment fixed by Allah.

kanz.f: How is Zina (adultery) defined?
kanz.b: Intercourse in the vagina, free from ownership or shubhah (a doubt of ownership).

kanz.f: What is the requirement for witness testimony in a Zina case?
kanz.b: Four witnesses who saw the act "like the kohl stick in the kohl container."

kanz.f: What is the procedure for a confession of Zina to be valid?
kanz.b: It must be confessed four times in four separate sessions, and the Imam should offer the chance to retract or suggest doubts.

kanz.f: Can a confession for Zina be retracted?
kanz.b: Yes, at any time before or during the punishment.

kanz.f: Who is subject to Rajm (stoning)?
kanz.b: Those who have previously engaged in a valid, lawful marriage (ihsan).

kanz.f: Who begins the execution of stoning?
kanz.b: The witnesses, followed by the Imam, then the people.

kanz.f: What is the punishment for an unmarried free person who commits Zina?
kanz.b: 100 lashes.

kanz.f: What is the punishment for a slave who commits Zina?
kanz.b: 50 lashes.

kanz.f: How should lashing be performed according to the protocol?
kanz.b: Using a medium whip without knots, with the man standing and the woman sitting; clothing is removed except for private parts (with padding for women).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on intercourse based on a legitimate shubhah (doubt)?
kanz.b: No Hadd is applied (e.g., intercourse with a slave owned by one's child, or a woman one believed to be his wife).

kanz.f: Does Hadd apply to intercourse with a slave owned by one's brother or paternal uncle, even if believed to be lawful?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Is Hadd applied if one has intercourse with a woman found in one's bed who is not one's wife?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Do acts of sodomy or bestiality trigger punishment?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Is Hadd applied for adultery committed in enemy territory?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Is Hadd applied for adultery committed by an intoxicated person?
kanz.b: Yes, if the intoxication was voluntary.

kanz.f: What happens to the Hadd if witnesses to Zina provide conflicting details?
kanz.b: The punishment is dropped.

kanz.f: What is the liability of witnesses if they retract their testimony after the Hadd has been carried out?
kanz.b: They must pay a share of the blood money (diyah).

kanz.f: What happens if witnesses retract their testimony before the Hadd is carried out?
kanz.b: The punishment is dropped, and the witnesses are punished instead.

kanz.f: What is the requirement for the Hadd penalty regarding drinking?
kanz.b: Drinking wine (khamr) or fermented liquor (nabidh) to the point of intoxication.

kanz.f: What is the required proof for the Hadd of drinking?
kanz.b: Two witnesses or one confession.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for drinking intoxicants for a free person?
kanz.b: 80 lashes.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for drinking intoxicants for a slave?
kanz.b: 40 lashes.

kanz.f: In what circumstances is the Hadd for drinking excluded?
kanz.b: If the smell has faded (without clear proof), if the person was forced, or if they were intoxicated to the point of total loss of sanity when they confessed.

kanz.f: What is Qadhf?
kanz.b: Falsely accusing someone of adultery.

kanz.f: What is the Hadd penalty for Qadhf?
kanz.b: 80 lashes for a free person.

kanz.f: What criteria must the victim meet to be considered muhsin (chaste)?
kanz.b: They must be an adult, free, Muslim, and sexually pure.

kanz.f: Besides explicit accusations of adultery, what else falls under Qadhf?
kanz.b: Denying someone's lineage (e.g., "You are not your father's son"), calling an Arab "non-Arab" (nabti), or accusing someone of incest.

kanz.f: If a person accuses someone whose mother is deceased, who may demand the Hadd punishment?
kanz.b: The mother's heirs.

kanz.f: Can a child demand punishment for the defamation of their father?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What happens to the Hadd if the victim of Qadhf dies?
kanz.b: The Hadd is voided.

kanz.f: Does the victim’s pardon or retraction of the accusation void the Hadd?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is Ta'zir?
kanz.b: A disciplinary punishment for offenses where no specific Hadd is fixed or where the conditions for Hadd are not fully met.

kanz.f: What are examples of offenses that warrant Ta'zir?
kanz.b: Insulting a slave or non-Muslim, using abusive language, or calling someone a sinner, disbeliever, thief, or hypocrite.

kanz.f: What is the maximum number of lashes for Ta'zir?
kanz.b: 39 lashes.

kanz.f: What is the minimum number of lashes for Ta'zir?
kanz.b: 3 lashes.

kanz.f: For what reasons may a husband discipline his wife?
kanz.b: Refusing to adorn herself, refusing marital relations, neglecting prayer or purification, or leaving the house without permission.

kanz.f: How is Sariqah (theft) defined?
kanz.b: The covert taking of property belonging to another, worth at least 10 dirhams, which was kept in a place of safe-keeping (hirz).

kanz.f: What is the penalty for a first offense of theft?
kanz.b: Amputation of the right hand from the wrist.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for a second offense of theft?
kanz.b: Amputation of the left foot.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for a third offense of theft?
kanz.b: Indefinite imprisonment until repentance.

kanz.f: What are examples of items that do not trigger amputation due to lack of canonical value?
kanz.b: Wood, grass, fish, birds, musical instruments, copies of the Quran, or non-valued items like wine.

kanz.f: Between which parties is amputation excluded for theft?
kanz.b: Close blood relatives, spouses, master and slave, or theft from public funds/shared property.

kanz.f: What constitutes Qat' at-Tariq (highway robbery)?
kanz.b: An armed or organized group blocking roads to take property.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for highway robbery involving only the taking of property?
kanz.b: Amputation of the hand and foot on opposite sides.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for highway robbery involving only murder?
kanz.b: Execution (Hadd), which cannot be pardoned by the victim's heirs.

kanz.f: What is the penalty for highway robbery involving both robbery and murder?
kanz.b: Execution and crucifixion, or either.

kanz.f: How is the crucifixion of a highway robber carried out?
kanz.b: The robber is crucified alive for three days.

kanz.f: When is the Hadd punishment for highway robbery not applied?
kanz.b: If it occurs within a city or involves close relatives (in these cases, Ta'zir or Qisas is applied).

kanz.f: What does the term Siyar refer to?
kanz.b: The plural of Sirah, referring to the methods of the Prophet ﷺ during his military campaigns.

kanz.f: Under normal conditions, what is the legal status of Jihad?
kanz.b: It is a communal obligation (fard kifayah).

kanz.f: When does Jihad become an individual obligation (fard ‘ayn)?
kanz.b: If the enemy attacks.

kanz.f: Who is exempt from the obligation of Jihad?
kanz.b: Children, women, slaves, the blind, the disabled, and the amputee.

kanz.f: What is the required protocol before commencing fighting?
kanz.b: Call the enemy to Islam; if they refuse, call them to pay Jizyah; if they refuse that, seek Allah's help and fight.

kanz.f: Is it permitted to destroy enemy fortifications or crops during a siege?
kanz.b: Yes, if necessary (e.g., using mangonels or drowning/burning fortifications).

kanz.f: What are the three primary prohibitions in Jihad?
kanz.b: Treachery (ghadr), stealing from the spoils (ghulul), and killing non-combatants (women, children, elderly, blind, disabled).

kanz.f: Under what circumstances can non-combatants be killed in war?
kanz.b: If they are actively participating in the war effort or are monarchs.

kanz.f: What are the two options for dealing with property seized by force?
kanz.b: Either dividing it among the soldiers or allowing the inhabitants to remain under the condition of paying Jizyah or Kharaj.

kanz.f: What are the Imam’s three options regarding prisoners of war?
kanz.b: Execute them, enslave them, or release them as a favor (mann).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on releasing prisoners back into enemy territory?
kanz.b: It is forbidden.

kanz.f: What is the share allocation for a foot soldier versus a cavalryman?
kanz.b: A foot soldier receives one share, and a cavalryman receives two.

kanz.f: Do slaves, women, and dhimmis serving in the army receive a full share of the spoils?
kanz.b: No, they receive a smaller gift (radkh).

kanz.f: Who is the Khums (one-fifth) of the spoils designated for?
kanz.b: Orphans, the needy, and wayfarers.

kanz.f: What is salab?
kanz.b: The personal belongings of an enemy soldier killed by a combatant, which the Imam may grant as an additional reward.

kanz.f: What is nafal in the context of military campaigns?
kanz.b: Additional rewards or bonuses granted by the Imam to specific soldiers or detachments.

kanz.f: If enemies seize our property and secure it in their territory, what is the status of ownership?
kanz.b: They become the legal owners of the property.

kanz.f: If we defeat the enemy, under what condition may one reclaim their own property for free?
kanz.b: If they find it before it is divided as spoils.

kanz.f: If one finds their property after it has been divided as spoils, what is required to reclaim it?
kanz.b: They must pay the price.

kanz.f: Do enemies gain ownership of free Muslims, mudabbar slaves, or mukattab (contracted) slaves?
kanz.b: No, they do not gain ownership of them.

kanz.f: Do enemies gain ownership of captured horses or other goods?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What is the status of a slave who flees to enemy territory?
kanz.b: The enemy does not gain ownership of him.

kanz.f: What is the rule for a merchant from our side entering enemy territory and taking property unlawfully?
kanz.b: He is prohibited from doing so; if he does, he must give it away in charity.

kanz.f: Is a debt between a harbi (warring party) and our merchant legally enforceable?
kanz.b: Generally no, unless both have converted to Islam after returning to our territory.

kanz.f: What happens if a musta'min remains in our territory for a full year?
kanz.b: He is treated as a dhimmi and must pay Jizyah.

kanz.f: If a musta'min converts to Islam while in our territory, what is the status of his young children?
kanz.b: They become free Muslims.

kanz.f: What is the status of property a musta'min entrusted to Muslims or dhimmis before converting?
kanz.b: It remains his property.

kanz.f: What happens to the property of a musta'min that is left in enemy territory upon his conversion?
kanz.b: It is treated as spoils of war (fi') if that land is subsequently conquered.

kanz.f: What are the three categories of 'Ushri land?
kanz.b: 1. Land in the Arabian Peninsula; 2. Land whose owners converted to Islam; 3. Land conquered by force that was distributed among the soldiers.

kanz.f: What are the categories of Kharaji land?
kanz.b: The Sawad region, land conquered by force whose inhabitants remained, or land conquered by treaty.

kanz.f: How is Kharaj typically calculated?
kanz.b: Based on cultivation (e.g., a sa‘ and a dirham per jarib of sown land).

kanz.f: When is Kharaj waived?
kanz.b: If water is unavailable, the harvest is destroyed by pests, or the land is rendered unusable.

kanz.f: Is 'Ushr (tithe) applied to Kharaji land?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the standard rate of 'Ushr applied to 'Ushri land?
Who is eligible to pay Jizyah?
kanz.b: The People of the Book (Jews, Christians), Zoroastrians, and polytheists who are non-Arabs.

kanz.f: Who is exempt from paying Jizyah?
kanz.b: Arabs (who are Muslim), apostates, children, women, slaves, mukattabs, the disabled, the blind, the poor (non-working), and isolated monks.

kanz.f: What are the yearly rates for Jizyah based on economic class?
kanz.b: 12 dirhams (poor worker), 24 dirhams (middle class), and 48 dirhams (wealthy).

kanz.f: What are the social restrictions placed on Dhimmis?
kanz.b: They must be distinguished by their attire, cannot ride horses, cannot carry weapons, and cannot build new places of worship (but may repair old ones).

kanz.f: What specific action voids the Dhimmi status?
kanz.b: Joining enemy territory to wage war (harabah); at this point, they are treated as apostates.

kanz.f: Does refusing to pay Jizyah or committing crimes like adultery/murder void the Dhimmi status?
kanz.b: No, these do not void the status.

kanz.f: What is the procedure for dealing with an apostate?
kanz.b: They are invited to return to Islam, their doubts are addressed, and they are imprisoned for three days; if they do not repent, they are executed.

kanz.f: Does the penalty for apostasy differ by gender?
kanz.b: Yes; women are imprisoned until they repent, but they are not executed.

kanz.f: What is the status of an apostate’s ownership?
kanz.b: It is suspended.

kanz.f: What happens to an apostate’s property if they repent?
kanz.b: They regain their property.

kanz.f: How are an apostate's earnings divided if they die or are executed while in apostasy?
kanz.b: Earnings made as a Muslim go to their Muslim heirs (after debts are paid), and earnings made as an apostate become public property (fi').

kanz.f: How are Bughat (rebels) defined in Islamic law?
kanz.b: Muslims who revolt against the Imam and seize territory.

kanz.f: What is the required policy of the Imam toward rebels?
kanz.b: He must invite them back to obedience and address their grievances; if they refuse, he fights them.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding rebel combatants who are wounded or retreating?
kanz.b: They are not to be pursued or killed.

kanz.f: Can the children of rebels be enslaved?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is the status of rebel property during the revolt?
kanz.b: It is sequestered (held), but not confiscated, until they repent.

kanz.f: What is the legal status of a foundling?
kanz.b: They are considered a free Muslim.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for the expenses of a foundling?
kanz.b: The public treasury (Bayt al-Mal).

kanz.f: Who inherits from a foundling if they have no heirs?
kanz.b: The public treasury (Bayt al-Mal).

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding a claim of lineage over a foundling?
kanz.b: If someone claims a foundling as their child, the lineage is established.

kanz.f: In the case of multiple claims of lineage for a foundling, how is the preference determined?
kanz.b: The claimant who provides specific identifying marks for the child is given preference.

kanz.f: What are the three things a finder is strictly prohibited from doing to a foundling?
kanz.b: They cannot marry them, sell them, or hire them out.

kanz.f: What responsibilities does the finder have regarding the foundling?
kanz.b: They must ensure the child is taught a trade and manage their affairs.

kanz.f: What is the legal status of Luqata (found property)?
kanz.b: It is a trust (amanah).

kanz.f: What must the finder do when taking possession of found property?
kanz.b: Call witnesses and announce the find until it becomes clear the owner will not seek it.

kanz.f: If a wealthy finder gives found property in charity and the owner later appears, what are the owner's options?
kanz.b: They may either ratify the charity or demand compensation from the finder.

kanz.f: What is the rule for managing stray animals that are found?
kanz.b: The finder may care for them; if they have utility, they may be rented out to cover maintenance costs; otherwise, they may be sold.

kanz.f: Can a finder withhold a found animal from the owner?
kanz.b: Yes, until maintenance costs are reimbursed.

kanz.f: Is it mandatory to return an item to a claimant who correctly describes its identifying marks?
kanz.b: It is permissible, but not mandatory.

kanz.f: What reward is a person entitled to for returning a runaway slave from a journey?
kanz.b: 40 dirhams (or a proportional amount for shorter distances).

kanz.f: What is the liability of the person returning a slave if the slave runs away again?
kanz.b: They are not liable, provided they bear witness that they took the slave specifically to return them.

kanz.f: How is a missing person (mafqud) defined?
kanz.b: Someone whose location, life, or death is unknown.

kanz.f: What is the responsibility of the judge regarding the property and family of a missing person?
kanz.b: The judge appoints an administrator to safeguard their property and support their dependents (parents, children, spouse).

kanz.f: Can the judge dissolve the marriage of a missing person?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: After how many years is a missing person legally declared dead?
kanz.b: 90 years.

kanz.f: What happens to the estate and marriage of a missing person once they are declared dead?
kanz.b: The wife observes the waiting period ('iddah), and the estate is distributed among the heirs.

kanz.f: Does a missing person inherit from others or allow others to inherit from them while they are still missing?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: How is inheritance managed if a missing person's presence affects the shares of other heirs?
kanz.b: The heirs receive the minimum possible share, and the remainder is held in reserve.

kanz.f: What is Sharikah al-Milk (Ownership Partnership)?
kanz.b: A partnership where two people own an asset together through inheritance or purchase.

kanz.f: What is Sharikah al-'Aqd (Contractual Partnership)?
kanz.b: A formal agreement between parties to share in a venture.

kanz.f: What are the requirements for Mufawadah (Equal Partnership)?
kanz.b: Equality in capital, agency, and liability.

kanz.f: Why is Mufawadah invalid between a free person and a slave, or a Muslim and a non-Muslim?
kanz.b: Because it requires equality in liability, which is not possible given their differing legal statuses.

kanz.f: In Mufawadah, what is the extent of a partner's liability?
kanz.b: Each partner is fully liable for the other's business obligations.

kanz.f: What characterizes 'Inan (Limited Partnership)?
kanz.b: Partners share in capital and profit (not necessarily equally), involving agency, but not universal liability.

kanz.f: What factors void a partnership agreement?
kanz.b: The death of a partner or the destruction of the capital.

kanz.f: How is Waqf (endowment) defined?
kanz.b: The retention of a specific asset ('ayn) and the dedication of its benefits to a charitable cause.

kanz.f: When does an owner's proprietary right over an asset cease during a Waqf?
kanz.b: Upon a judicial decree.

kanz.f: What are the requirements for the purpose of an endowment?
kanz.b: It must be a permanent, non-terminating entity.

kanz.f: Does the founder of a Waqf have any control over the asset after endowment?
kanz.b: Yes, the founder may reserve the right to manage the endowment or the income for themselves.

kanz.f: Can a manager (mutawalli) be removed if the founder stipulated that they could not be removed?
kanz.b: Yes, the judge may remove them for dishonesty despite the founder's stipulation.

kanz.f: When is a mosque legally established as a Waqf?
kanz.b: When the builder separates it from their property and permits public prayer.

kanz.f: What is the status of a mosque built inside a private home with restricted access?
kanz.b: The founder retains ownership and may sell or bequeath it (it is not a public Waqf).

kanz.f: How is a sale (Bay') defined?
kanz.b: The exchange of property for property by mutual consent.

kanz.f: What are the two ways a sale is finalized?
kanz.b: Offer and acceptance, or by ta'ati (mutual exchange without verbal agreement).

kanz.f: What happens if a party leaves the gathering before the offer is accepted?
kanz.b: The offer becomes void.

kanz.f: What is the requirement for pricing in a sale?
kanz.b: The price must be known in both amount and description.

kanz.f: If the currency type is not specified in a contract, what is assumed?
kanz.b: The prevalent local currency.

kanz.f: In what two ways can food be sold?
kanz.b: By weight/measure or by bulk (jaza'an).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on selling a pile of goods by the sa' at a set price per sa'?
kanz.b: The sale is valid for the amount measured.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on selling an entire lot (e.g., a flock of sheep) at a price per unit?
kanz.b: If the total is not specified, the contract is void; if the total is named, it is valid.

kanz.f: In the sale of a house, what items are implied to be included?
kanz.b: The structure and the keys.

kanz.f: In the sale of land, what is implied to be included?
kanz.b: The trees on the land.

kanz.f: Are crops on land or fruits on trees automatically included in a sale?
kanz.b: No, they are excluded unless explicitly stated.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding the sale of fruits on trees?
kanz.b: They must be cut immediately; it is invalid to stipulate that they remain on the trees.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for measurement costs in a sale?
kanz.b: The seller.

kanz.f: Who is responsible for currency weighing and payment costs?
kanz.b: The buyer.

kanz.f: What is the Khiyar ash-Shart (Option of Condition)?
kanz.b: An option stipulated by the parties to rescind the sale within a set period (maximum three days).

kanz.f: How does the seller's option affect ownership?
kanz.b: It prevents the sale from transferring ownership away from the seller.

kanz.f: If a buyer takes possession of an item during the seller's option period, what is their liability?
kanz.b: They are liable for the value of the item if it is damaged.

kanz.f: How does a buyer's option affect ownership?
kanz.b: It does not prevent ownership from transferring to the buyer, but the buyer remains liable for the price if damaged.

kanz.f: What events void an option of condition?
kanz.b: Death, expiration of time, manumission of the item, or exercising a right of pre-emption (shuf'ah).

kanz.f: What is Khiyar ar-Ru'yah (Option of Inspection)?
kanz.b: The right of a buyer to rescind a sale of an unseen item upon seeing it, even if they had agreed to it beforehand.

kanz.f: Who possesses the Khiyar ar-Ru'yah?
kanz.b: Only the buyer; the seller does not have this option.

kanz.f: What constitutes sufficient inspection for goods like grain, animals, cloth, and houses?
kanz.b: Sight is sufficient for piles of grain, animals (including their backsides), cloth (exterior), and the interior of a house.

kanz.f: What is the Khiyar al-'Ayb (Option of Defect)?
kanz.b: The right of a buyer to return goods or accept them for the full price if a defect reducing their value is discovered.

kanz.f: What are examples of defects in slaves mentioned in the text?
kanz.b: Running away, bedwetting, theft, foul breath, adultery, pregnancy, or lack of menstruation.

kanz.f: If an item is altered or consumed after purchase, what is the buyer's recourse for a defect?
kanz.b: They may only claim the difference in value caused by the defect, rather than returning the item.

kanz.f: What happens if an item is consumed or destroyed before a defect is claimed?
kanz.b: No claim for the defect remains.

kanz.f: Does using an item (riding, wearing, treating) always constitute acceptance of a defect?
kanz.b: Yes, unless the use was for returning the item or providing necessary care.

kanz.f: What are examples of items whose sale is fundamentally prohibited?
kanz.b: Carrion, blood, swine, wine, free people, umm al-walad, mudabbar slaves, or mukattabs.

kanz.f: Why are sales of fish before capture, birds in the air, or a fetus in the womb considered invalid?
kanz.b: Because they involve excessive uncertainty (gharar) regarding the existence or accessibility of the object.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to sell leather, bones, or nerves from carrion?
kanz.b: Yes, provided they have been tanned or processed.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding sales that include extraneous conditions (e.g., selling a house on the condition that the seller lives in it)?
kanz.b: The sale is invalid.

kanz.f: Are there exceptions for service-related conditions in a sale?
kanz.b: Yes, services that are part of the craft (e.g., a cobbler stitching a shoe he sold) are permissible.

kanz.f: What is the status of sales contingent on vague future events (e.g., "when the pilgrims arrive")?
kanz.b: They are invalid.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to enter into a guarantee (kafalah) tied to a future event?
kanz.b: Yes, guarantees are permitted even if tied to such times.

kanz.f: In an invalid sale, what is the buyer's status if they take possession with the seller’s order?
kanz.b: The buyer becomes the owner upon paying the value.

kanz.f: Until what point may either party rescind an invalid sale?
kanz.b: Until the buyer alters, gives away, emancipates, or builds upon the item.

kanz.f: Who is entitled to keep profits earned from an invalid sale?
kanz.b: The seller may keep them, but the buyer may not.

kanz.f: What is Najash and what is its legal status?
kanz.b: Bidding up an item without the intent to buy; it is makruh (disliked).

kanz.f: What is talaqqi al-jalb?
kanz.b: Intercepting caravans to purchase goods before they reach the market.

kanz.f: Which practices are considered makruh (disliked) in the context of trade?
kanz.b: Najash, bidding on someone else's offer, talaqqi al-jalb, selling by a resident for an outsider, and selling during the Friday prayer call.

kanz.f: What is Iqalah?
kanz.b: A mutual cancellation of a sale by the parties involved.

kanz.f: How is Iqalah treated in relation to the parties versus third parties?
kanz.b: It is treated as a rescission between the parties, but as a new sale in relation to third parties.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding the price during Iqalah?
kanz.b: It must be for the original price; a higher or lower price makes the Iqalah void.

kanz.f: What happens if the item being returned in Iqalah is destroyed?
kanz.b: The Iqalah is voided.

kanz.f: What happens if the price (the money) is destroyed during an Iqalah?
kanz.b: It does not void the Iqalah.

kanz.f: What is Tawliyah?
kanz.b: Reselling an item at the original cost price.

kanz.f: What is Murabahah?
kanz.b: Reselling an item at cost plus an agreed-upon profit.

kanz.f: Can a seller include labor costs (e.g., shepherding, teaching) in the base cost of a Murabahah sale?
kanz.b: No; they may only include ancillary costs like dyeing, transport, or spinning.

kanz.f: What is the buyer's recourse if the seller lies about the original cost in a Murabahah sale?
kanz.b: The buyer may either return the item or demand a price reduction.

kanz.f: Can real estate be sold before taking physical possession?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Can movable property be sold before taking possession?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is required before the resale or consumption of items sold by weight or measure?
kanz.b: They must be physically weighed or measured.

kanz.f: How is Riba (usury) defined?
kanz.b: An unjustified excess in an exchange of goods.

kanz.f: To which types of goods does Riba apply?
kanz.b: Goods measured by volume (e.g., grain, dates, salt) or by weight (e.g., gold, silver).

kanz.f: What is the rule when exchanging items of the same genus?
kanz.b: Equality is required; unequal amounts are forbidden.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding the timing of payments for items of the same genus?
kanz.b: Deferment is forbidden; payment must be immediate.

kanz.f: When is it permissible to exchange unequal amounts of goods?
kanz.b: When the genera are different.

kanz.f: How should goods of different genera but similar categories (e.g., gold for silver) be exchanged?
kanz.b: Hand-to-hand (immediately), though amounts may be unequal.

kanz.f: Are there any exceptions to the rules of Riba?
kanz.b: Yes, no Riba exists between a master and their slave, or between a Muslim and a harbi (enemy combatant) in enemy territory.

kanz.f: Are secondary rights (e.g., right-of-way, drainage) included in the sale of a house or land by default?
kanz.b: No, they must be explicitly specified (e.g., "with all its rights").

kanz.f: How do rights in a lease (ijarah) differ from those in a sale?
kanz.b: In a lease, these rights are generally understood to be included.

kanz.f: What is the difference between bayyinah (evidence) and iqrar (admission) in terms of transferability?
kanz.b: Bayyinah is a transferable proof, whereas iqrar is not.

kanz.f: Do contradictory claims regarding ownership prevent a lawsuit?
kanz.b: Yes, except for cases involving freedom, divorce, or lineage.

kanz.f: If a buyer purchases a slave who claims to be free, from whom can the buyer recover their price?
kanz.b: The seller.

kanz.f: If a slave induces a purchase through fraud, what is the buyer's recourse?
kanz.b: They may seek recourse against the slave.

kanz.f: What is Bay' al-Fuduli (Unauthorized Sale)?
kanz.b: The sale of another person's property by an unauthorized person.

kanz.f: What determines the validity of Bay' al-Fuduli?
kanz.b: It is contingent upon the owner's subsequent approval.

kanz.f: In Bay' al-Fuduli, who receives compensation if the item is injured while in the buyer's possession?
kanz.b: The buyer (provided the owner later approves the sale).

kanz.f: What happens to the excess profit if a Fuduli sale is made for more than the item's value?
kanz.b: The excess is given as charity.

kanz.f: How is a Salam (Advance Sale) defined?
kanz.b: A sale of goods for immediate payment with future delivery.

kanz.f: For which types of goods is a Salam contract valid?
kanz.b: Items whose quality and quantity can be precisely defined (measured, weighed, or counted).

kanz.f: Why is Salam invalid for livestock, jewels, or fresh fish?
kanz.b: Because these items possess inconsistent quality that cannot be precisely defined.

kanz.f: What are the three core conditions for a valid Salam contract?
kanz.b: 1) Payment must be made in full before separating; 2) Delivery time must be specified (minimum one month); 3) Quality and quantity must be clearly defined.

kanz.f: What is Istisna' (Manufacturing), and what right does the buyer retain?
kanz.b: A contract for made-to-order items (like shoes or pots); the buyer retains the right of inspection upon delivery.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to sell animals like dogs, leopards, birds of prey, or insects?
kanz.b: Yes, these may be legally sold.

kanz.f: Which types of contracts are voided by the inclusion of invalid conditions?
kanz.b: Sales, leasing, and partnerships.

kanz.f: Which types of contracts are not voided by invalid conditions (but instead, the condition is ignored)?
kanz.b: Marriage, divorce, manumission, and loans.

kanz.f: Where does collateral (rahn) remain according to the rules of this text?
kanz.b: It remains with the mortgagee.

kanz.f: If a person is owed a specific currency but accepts debased coins instead, is the debt considered satisfied?
kanz.b: Yes, the debt is considered satisfied.

kanz.f: What is Sarf?
kanz.b: The exchange of one form of legal tender (gold/silver/currency) for another.

kanz.f: What are the two requirements for exchanging the same genus (e.g., gold for gold)?
kanz.b: Equality in weight and immediate, hand-to-hand possession (taqabud) at the session.

kanz.f: What is the requirement for exchanging different genera (e.g., gold for silver)?
kanz.b: Immediate, hand-to-hand possession (taqabud), but not equality of weight.

kanz.f: What happens if two parties separate before the currency is fully possessed?
kanz.b: The contract is void.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to dispose of currency before taking physical possession of it?
kanz.b: No, it is invalid.

kanz.f: How are gold or silver with a high percentage of adulteration (ghash) treated in Sarf?
kanz.b: They are treated as commodities, so they may be sold for their own genus with a price difference (usury laws of equality do not apply).

kanz.f: How is Kafalah (Suretyship) defined?
kanz.b: The addition of one person's liability to another's regarding a claim.

kanz.f: What is Kafalah bi-an-Nafs (Surety of Person)?
kanz.b: An agreement where the surety takes responsibility for producing the debtor when requested.

kanz.f: What is the consequence if the surety fails to produce the debtor in a Kafalah bi-an-Nafs?
kanz.b: The judge may imprison the surety.

kanz.f: When is a Kafalah bi-an-Nafs voided?
kanz.b: By the death of either the debtor or the surety.

kanz.f: What is Kafalah bi-al-Mal (Surety of Debt)?
kanz.b: An agreement where the surety takes responsibility for paying a debt.

kanz.f: Is Kafalah bi-al-Mal valid if the debt amount is currently unknown?
kanz.b: Yes, provided it is a valid, binding debt.

kanz.f: Can a surety seek reimbursement if they pay a debt without the debtor's order?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: If a creditor releases the original debtor, what happens to the surety?
kanz.b: The surety is also released.

kanz.f: Does releasing the surety release the original debtor?
kanz.b: No, the debtor remains liable.

kanz.f: If two debtors mutually guarantee each other, how much can one seek in reimbursement after paying the debt?
kanz.b: Only the amount that exceeds his own half of the debt.

kanz.f: In a mutual guarantee, from whom may the creditor demand the full debt?
kanz.b: From either party.

kanz.f: Is a slave's suretyship for his master binding?
kanz.b: Yes, if done by the master's order.

kanz.f: If a slave pays a debt for his master and later becomes free, can he seek reimbursement?
kanz.b: No, he may not seek reimbursement from the master.

kanz.f: What is Hawalah?
kanz.b: The transfer of a debt from one person's liability to another's.

kanz.f: Can Hawalah be applied to specific physical assets ('ayn)?
kanz.b: No, it is valid only for debts.

kanz.f: Which three parties must consent to a Hawalah?
kanz.b: The transferor (muhil), the transferee (muhtal), and the person who accepts the debt (muhal 'alayh).

kanz.f: What is the status of the original debtor upon the acceptance of a Hawalah?
kanz.b: They are released from the debt.

kanz.f: In what two scenarios can a transferee seek recourse from the original debtor after a Hawalah?
kanz.b: If the new debtor denies the Hawalah and swears an oath, or if the new debtor dies insolvent.

kanz.f: If a debt is transferred against a deposit held by a third party, and that deposit is later destroyed, what happens to the transferor?
kanz.b: The transferor is released from the debt.

kanz.f: What are the essential qualifications for a judge (Qadi)?
kanz.b: Trustworthy, chaste, intelligent, pious, and knowledgeable in the Sunnah and fiqh.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to appoint a corrupt person as a judge?
kanz.b: It is technically possible but highly discouraged; a judge who takes bribes must be removed.

kanz.f: What are some requirements for a judge's conduct to ensure impartiality?
kanz.b: Avoiding private sessions with litigants, rejecting special invitations, and not prompting witnesses.

kanz.f: If a debtor claims poverty when ordered to pay, what is the judge’s procedure?
kanz.b: The judge investigates; if no wealth is found, the debtor is released; if wealthy, they may be imprisoned until payment.

kanz.f: In which cases are letters between judges not accepted as testimony?
kanz.b: Cases involving Hadd (fixed penalties) or Qisas (retaliation).

kanz.f: How does the receiving judge verify a letter from another judge?
kanz.b: By opening it in the presence of the defendant and witnesses to confirm its authenticity.

kanz.f: Under what conditions does an inter-judicial letter become void?
kanz.b: If the issuing or receiving judge dies or is dismissed, unless addressed to "any judge who receives this."

kanz.f: What disputes are excluded from the scope of Tahkim (arbitration)?
kanz.b: Cases involving Hadd (fixed penalties), Qisas (retaliation), or diyah (blood money).

kanz.f: When is an arbitrator's ruling binding?
kanz.b: When the arbitrator is qualified to be a judge and the ruling does not contradict the established school of law.

kanz.f: Can an arbitrator rule in favor of their own family members?
kanz.b: No, they cannot rule in favor of their parents, children, or spouse.

kanz.f: If a person claims an inheritance for themselves and an absent brother, what share are they granted?
kanz.b: They are only granted their own share, provided they have evidence.

kanz.f: Does a bequest of "one-third of my property" apply only to specific assets or the entire estate?
kanz.b: It applies to the entire estate.

kanz.f: How does the appointment of an executor (wasi) differ from an agent (wakil) regarding notification?
kanz.b: An executor is considered appointed even if unaware of the appointment, whereas an agent's authority only begins upon notification.

kanz.f: Is a judicial order enforceable if the defendant acknowledges the facts?
kanz.b: Yes, if the order was issued by a qualified judge.

kanz.f: How is Shahadah (testimony) defined?
kanz.b: A report based on direct observation, not speculation.

kanz.f: What is the required number of witnesses for Zina (adultery)?
kanz.b: Four men.

kanz.f: What is the required number of witnesses for Hadd or Qisas cases?
kanz.b: Two men.

kanz.f: In matters of women (e.g., birth, virginity), what testimony is sufficient?
kanz.b: One woman.

kanz.f: For general financial or civil matters, what is the required witness structure?
kanz.b: Two men, or one man and two women.

kanz.f: Who is ineligible to provide testimony?
kanz.b: The blind, slaves, minors, the person punished for qadhf (false accusation), parents, spouses, masters, and business partners (in partnership matters).

kanz.f: Does the law accept testimony from non-Muslims (dhimmis)?
kanz.b: Yes, against others of their own faith.

kanz.f: Which conduct-based actions disqualify a witness?
kanz.b: Major sins, consuming riba (usury), gambling (dice, chess), or public immorality.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding the alignment of testimony and the plaintiff's claim?
kanz.b: Testimony must align with the claim; if it contradicts the claim (e.g., inheritance vs. purchase), it is rejected.

kanz.f: What happens if witnesses disagree on the numerical amount involved (e.g., one says 1,000, another says 2,000)?
kanz.b: The testimony is rejected.

kanz.f: What is the consequence if witnesses report contradictory circumstances (e.g., different locations for a crime)?
kanz.b: The testimony is void.

kanz.f: What is Shahadah 'ala ash-Shahadah?
kanz.b: Testimony on testimony: where secondary witnesses testify to the testimony of primary witnesses.

kanz.f: In what types of cases is Shahadah 'ala ash-Shahadah permissible?
kanz.b: In civil cases (where uncertainty does not void the penalty).

kanz.f: Under what conditions may secondary witnesses (far') testify?
kanz.b: Only if the primary witnesses (asl) are dead, ill, or traveling.

kanz.f: What is required for the validation of Shahadah 'ala ash-Shahadah?
kanz.b: The primary witnesses must have explicitly asked the secondary witnesses to bear testimony on their behalf.

kanz.f: What happens if the primary witness denies having authorized the secondary testimony?
kanz.b: The secondary testimony is void.

kanz.f: Where must a retraction of testimony take place to be valid?
kanz.b: In the presence of a judge.

kanz.f: What is the effect of a witness retracting their testimony before the judge's ruling?
kanz.b: The ruling is not issued.

kanz.f: What is the effect of a witness retracting their testimony after the judge's ruling?
kanz.b: The ruling is not overturned.

kanz.f: If a witness retracts after the plaintiff has already obtained the property, who is liable?
kanz.b: The retracting witness is liable for damages to the defendant.

kanz.f: How is liability shared if one of two witnesses retracts?
kanz.b: The retracting witness is liable for half of the damages.

kanz.f: In Shahadah 'ala ash-Shahadah, who is liable if a secondary witness (far') retracts?
kanz.b: The secondary witness (far'), not the original witness (asl).

kanz.f: What is the definition of Wakalah (Agency)?
kanz.b: Appointing another person to act on one's behalf in permissible matters.

kanz.f: Who is eligible to act as an agent?
kanz.b: Anyone capable of understanding the contract, including minors or slaves.

kanz.f: In what scope may an agent act on behalf of a principal?
kanz.b: In all matters that the principal is legally capable of performing themselves.

kanz.f: In "Direct Agency" (e.g., sales, leasing), who is bound by the contract and where does ownership vest?
kanz.b: The contract binds the agent, but ownership vests in the principal.

kanz.f: In "Attributed Agency" (e.g., marriage, khul'), who is bound by the contract?
kanz.b: The principal is bound directly; the agent is not held liable for the results.

kanz.f: What must an agent do regarding price and item type according to the principal's instructions?
kanz.b: Follow the principal's explicit instructions precisely.

kanz.f: If an agent buys an item different from the specific one requested, to whom does the purchase belong?
kanz.b: To the agent, unless they intended it for the principal or used the principal's funds.

kanz.f: In a dispute over whether a purchase was made for the principal or the agent, whose word is accepted?
kanz.b: The principal's word.

kanz.f: What is a restriction on the agent regarding whom they can sell to?
kanz.b: The agent may not sell to individuals whose testimony would be rejected if given in the agent's favor (e.g., close relatives).

kanz.f: Does an agent appointed for litigation (khusamah) automatically have the right to collect debts?
kanz.b: No, they require explicit authorization for collections.

kanz.f: If a debtor pays a debt to someone claiming to be an agent who lacks authorization, what is the outcome?
kanz.b: The debtor may be forced to pay again to the principal, though they may seek recourse from the false agent.

kanz.f: Is it permissible to surrender a deposit (wadi'ah) to someone claiming to be an agent?
kanz.b: No, proof of authorization is required.

kanz.f: What is the term for the dismissal of an agent?
kanz.b: 'Azl (عزل).

kanz.f: When does a dismissal by the principal become effective?
kanz.b: Upon the agent's knowledge of the dismissal.

kanz.f: Besides dismissal by the principal, what are three other events that void an agency?
kanz.b: Death of either party, insanity of either party, or the principal performing the action themselves.

kanz.f: How does the apostasy of the principal affect an agency?
kanz.b: It voids the agency if the apostasy results in joining enemy territory.

kanz.f: If a principal becomes a restricted slave or bankrupt, what happens to their agent?
kanz.b: The agency is voided due to the principal's incapacity.

kanz.f: If an agency is linked to a partnership, what happens if that partnership is dissolved?
kanz.b: The agency is voided.

kanz.f: How is a Da'wa (claim) defined?
kanz.b: The attribution of a right to oneself during a dispute.

kanz.f: Who is the plaintiff (mudda'i) in a dispute?
kanz.b: The one who would not be compelled to pursue the matter if they remained silent.

kanz.f: What specific details must be provided in a claim for real estate?
kanz.b: The boundaries and the names of the neighbors.

kanz.f: What is the procedure if a defendant denies the plaintiff's claim?
kanz.b: The plaintiff must provide evidence (bayyinah). If they lack evidence, the defendant is asked to take an oath.

kanz.f: What is nukul in the context of a judicial claim?
kanz.b: The defendant's refusal to take an oath; judgment may be passed against them upon this refusal.

kanz.f: By what must oaths be sworn?
kanz.b: By the name of Allah.

kanz.f: In which types of cases is the oath not administered?
kanz.b: In matters of Hadd (fixed punishment) or certain family laws.

kanz.f: What is the status of a claim if the defendant pays to avoid an oath or settles?
kanz.b: The matter is concluded.

kanz.f: What is the procedure (tahalluf) when parties disagree on the price or subject of a sale and lack evidence?
kanz.b: Both parties take oaths, starting with the buyer, after which either may request the judge to annul the contract.

kanz.f: If parties disagree on the duration (delay) or conditions (options) of a sale, whose word is accepted?
kanz.b: The word of the denier, provided they are supported by an oath.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if two people provide evidence of ownership for an item held by a third party?
kanz.b: The item is divided between them.

kanz.f: In conflicting claims of ownership, which evidence prevails regarding dates?
kanz.b: Evidence of a specific date prevails over undated evidence.

kanz.f: Between evidence of a sale and evidence of a gift, which generally outranks the other?
kanz.b: Purchase and sale evidence generally outranks gift evidence.

kanz.f: If two people provide evidence of purchasing the same item from the same seller, what is the ruling?
kanz.b: They share the item.

kanz.f: Who is presumed to have the stronger claim regarding physical property?
kanz.b: The person currently in physical possession (or riding/wearing the item).

kanz.f: What is the "Six-Month Rule" regarding a sold slave-woman who gives birth?
kanz.b: If birth occurs within less than six months of sale, the seller's claim to the child is valid; the sale is annulled, the woman becomes his umm al-walad, and the price is returned.

kanz.f: Does the "Six-Month Rule" apply if the buyer also claims the child?
kanz.b: Yes, it still applies.

kanz.f: What happens if the mother dies after a claim of lineage is made?
kanz.b: The claim for the child's lineage still stands.

kanz.f: What happens if the child dies after a claim of lineage is made?
kanz.b: The claim for lineage is void.

kanz.f: If a slave-woman gives birth to twins and the seller claims only one, what is the status of the other?
kanz.b: The lineage of both twins is established.

kanz.f: If a slave-woman is sold and gives birth to a child by the seller, what is the status of the child?
kanz.b: The child is born free, and the seller must compensate the buyer for the price and the child’s value.

kanz.f: How is Iqrar (Acknowledgement/Confession) defined?
kanz.b: Informing of a right due to others from oneself.

kanz.f: What are the essential conditions for a person making an Iqrar?
kanz.b: They must be a free, accountable adult.

kanz.f: What is the rule if one makes an ambiguous acknowledgment, such as "I owe you 'something'"?
kanz.b: The acknowledgment is valid, but the person must clarify the amount.

kanz.f: In legal terms, how much is the "much" (kathir) often defined as when referring to money?
kanz.b: Ten (units of currency).

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding partial exceptions (e.g., "I owe you 100 except 20")?
kanz.b: It is valid if done immediately (mutassilan).

kanz.f: What happens if an entire amount is excluded via an exception?
kanz.b: The exception is void.

kanz.f: What is the effect of attaching "Insha'Allah" to an acknowledgment?
kanz.b: It nullifies the acknowledgment.

kanz.f: If an acknowledgment cites an invalid cause (e.g., wine or pork), what is the status of the debt?
kanz.b: The specific obligation is void, though some general debts may remain binding.

kanz.f: Regarding debt priority, how are debts from health and those acknowledged during a fatal illness treated?
kanz.b: Debts incurred during health take precedence over those acknowledged during a fatal illness.

kanz.f: Is an acknowledgment of debt made to an heir during a fatal illness valid?
kanz.b: It is void unless the other heirs consent.

kanz.f: Are acknowledgments of debt to strangers during a fatal illness valid?
kanz.b: Yes, they are valid.

kanz.f: Under what condition is an acknowledgment of a child during a fatal illness valid?
kanz.b: It is valid if it establishes lineage and the person is someone who could realistically be their child.

kanz.f: How is Sulh (Settlement/Compromise) defined?
kanz.b: A contract to resolve a dispute.

kanz.f: How is a settlement based on admission legally treated?
kanz.b: As a sale (subject to rules like pre-emption and return for defects).

kanz.f: How is a settlement based on denial or silence treated?
kanz.b: As a ransom for an oath (for the denier) or an exchange (for the plaintiff).

kanz.f: In which cases is a settlement invalid?
kanz.b: In cases involving Hadd (fixed punishments).

kanz.f: If an agent settles a claim without explicit authorization, when is it valid?
kanz.b: It is valid only if the agent guarantees the payment; otherwise, it is contingent on the principal's approval.

kanz.f: In Sulh fi ad-Dayn (settlement of debt), is settling for a portion of the original debt considered a trade?
kanz.b: No, it is considered an abandonment (ibra') of the remainder.

kanz.f: What are the restrictions on settling a debt of 1,000 for 500?
kanz.b: It must be paid immediately, and it cannot involve different genres (like gold for silver) or create riba (usury).

kanz.f: If a creditor promises a release on the condition of paying half the debt by a specific time, is it valid?
kanz.b: Yes, provided the condition is met, the release is valid.

kanz.f: If two partners share a debt and one settles his portion for an asset, what rights does the other partner have?
kanz.b: They may either demand half the debt from the debtor or take half the asset from their partner (unless the partner guaranteed a portion of the debt).

kanz.f: What is the definition of Mudarabah?
kanz.b: A partnership where one party provides the capital and the other provides the labor.

kanz.f: What are the three legal roles of the Mudarib (worker)?
kanz.b: Trustee (amin), agent (wakil) for management, and profit-sharer.

kanz.f: What is the requirement for profit sharing in Mudarabah?
kanz.b: Profits must be shared proportionally (e.g., 50/50).

kanz.f: What happens if a Mudarabah contract stipulates a fixed lump sum for one party?
kanz.b: The contract is invalid, and the worker is instead entitled to the "fair wage" (ajr al-mithl).

kanz.f: Are conditions that create ambiguity regarding profit distribution valid?
kanz.b: No, they are invalid.

kanz.f: What are the restrictions on the worker (Mudarib) regarding trade?
kanz.b: They cannot trade outside the specified conditions (time, place, goods) set by the capital owner.

kanz.f: Can a Mudarib delegate the management of capital to a second Mudarib?
kanz.b: No, not without the capital owner’s permission.

kanz.f: In Mudarabah, how are losses handled?
kanz.b: Losses are deducted from the profit.

kanz.f: Is a Mudarib liable if losses exceed the capital?
kanz.b: No, they are not liable (as they are a trustee) unless they acted negligently or violated the contract.

kanz.f: When can a Mudarib charge their living expenses (food, clothing, etc.) to the capital?
kanz.b: When they are traveling for the Mudarabah.

kanz.f: If a Mudarib is working in their own city, who covers their living expenses?
kanz.b: The Mudarib covers their own expenses.

kanz.f: What is the nature of a deposit (Wadi'ah)?
kanz.b: It is a trust (amanah).

kanz.f: When is a trustee liable for the loss of a deposit?
kanz.b: When they are negligent or act against the owner's instructions.

kanz.f: Which actions cause a trustee to become liable for the whole of a deposit?
kanz.b: Refusing to return it when requested (while able), mixing it with their own property, or spending a portion.

kanz.f: If two people deposit an item, how should the trustee return it?
kanz.b: They must not return it to one without the other being present.

kanz.f: How should a trustee handle a divisible item deposited by two people?
kanz.b: They may split it and return the respective shares.

kanz.f: How should a trustee handle an indivisible item deposited by two people?
kanz.b: The trustee holds it until both are present.

kanz.f: How is 'Ariyah (Loan for Use) defined?
kanz.b: Granting the usufruct of an item without compensation.

kanz.f: Can the lender reclaim the borrowed item at any time?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: Is the borrower of an 'Ariyah item liable for damage if there is no negligence (ta'addi)?
kanz.b: No, the borrower is a trustee.

kanz.f: What are two things a borrower of an 'Ariyah item is prohibited from doing?
kanz.b: Leasing the item or pledging it as collateral.

kanz.f: If a borrower pledges an 'Ariyah item and it is subsequently damaged, what is the result?
kanz.b: The borrower becomes liable.

kanz.f: What must a borrower do if the loan is restricted to a specific time or purpose?
kanz.b: They must not exceed those restrictions.

kanz.f: If land is loaned for building or planting, what may the lender require upon reclaiming it?
kanz.b: The lender may require the borrower to remove the structures.

kanz.f: How is Hibah (Gift) defined?
kanz.b: Transferring ownership of an asset without compensation.

kanz.f: What are the three conditions required for a valid gift?
kanz.b: Offer (ijab), acceptance, and possession (qabd).

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding possession of a gift?
kanz.b: Gifts must be physically handed over.

kanz.f: What is required to make a gift of a divisible item (musha') valid?
kanz.b: It must be divided and separated to be valid.

kanz.f: Why is a gift from a father to his minor child complete immediately upon the contract?
kanz.b: Because the father acts as the child's guardian.

kanz.f: What is the mnemonic used to remember the impediments to revoking a gift?
kanz.b: "DAM' KH-Z-Q-H" (دمع خزقه).

kanz.f: What does the "D" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Ziyadah: Increase in the gift (e.g., planting trees on gifted land).

kanz.f: What does the "M" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Mawt: Death of one of the parties.

kanz.f: What does the "'" (Ayn) in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: 'Iwad: Receipt of a counter-gift or compensation.

kanz.f: What does the "KH" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Khuruj: Property leaving the donee’s ownership (e.g., selling half).

kanz.f: What does the "Z" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Zawjiyah: Existence of a marriage between the parties.

kanz.f: What does the "Q" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Qarabah: Close blood kinship (prohibiting marriage).

kanz.f: What does the "H" in DAM' KH-Z-Q-H represent?
kanz.b: Halak: Destruction of the gift.

kanz.f: How is Ijarah (Leasing/Hiring) defined?
kanz.b: Selling a known benefit for a known wage.

kanz.f: What are the three ways to determine the "known benefit" in a lease?
kanz.b: By time (e.g., housing), by specific task (e.g., dyeing), or by reference (e.g., transporting goods).

kanz.f: When is ownership of the wage established in Ijarah?
kanz.b: Through immediate payment, a condition of advance payment, full utilization, or the capacity to utilize the benefit.

kanz.f: Which craftsmen may hold the hired item until they are paid?
kanz.b: Craftsmen whose work leaves an effect on the item (e.g., dyers).

kanz.f: Which craftsmen are prohibited from holding the hired item for payment?
kanz.b: Craftsmen whose work does not leave an effect on the item (e.g., porters).

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding specifying activity when leasing houses and shops?
kanz.b: It is valid without specifying the exact activity, provided the use is not prohibited (e.g., furnace, blacksmith).

kanz.f: What is required when leasing land for agriculture?
kanz.b: Specification of the crop or a general statement like "plant whatever you wish."

kanz.f: What must happen to structures built on leased land upon the expiration of the lease?
kanz.b: They must be removed unless the lessor compensates the lessee for their value (in a "removed" state).

kanz.f: If a lease for an animal or garment is unrestricted, what are the lessee's rights?
kanz.b: The lessee may use it as they see fit.

kanz.f: In a restricted lease, when does the lessee become liable for damages?
kanz.b: If they exceed the restriction, cause harm, or change the nature of the burden (e.g., carrying salt instead of grain).

kanz.f: What is the consequence of using a leased animal on a different route than specified?
kanz.b: If it results in a difference in burden or causes damage, the lessee is liable.

kanz.f: What is the consequence of invalid conditions in an Ijarah contract?
kanz.b: The conditions (and thus the lease) are invalid; the lessee is entitled to the "fair wage" (ajr al-mithl) up to the amount originally agreed upon.

kanz.f: Is a lease of a house defined as "by the month for one dirham" valid for the long term?
kanz.b: It is valid for only one month unless the total duration is specified.

kanz.f: What is the rule regarding leasing for singing, lamentation, or forbidden entertainment?
kanz.b: The lease is invalid.

kanz.f: What is the status of fees for religious services (e.g., Azan, Hajj, Imamat)?
kanz.b: It is a subject of legal debate; however, contemporary fatwa allows leasing for Quranic education.

kanz.f: What is a Common Employee (Al-Ajir al-Mushtarak)?
kanz.b: A worker who works for multiple people (e.g., dyer, fuller).

kanz.f: When is a Common Employee liable for the loss of items?
kanz.b: Only if the loss results from their own work (e.g., tearing fabric while beating it, a porter slipping).

kanz.f: Are Common Employees liable for accidental destruction of items not caused by their labor?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What is an Exclusive Employee (Al-Ajir al-Khass)?
kanz.b: An employee hired for a specific period (e.g., for a month).

kanz.f: When does an Exclusive Employee become entitled to their wage?
kanz.b: Once they make themselves available, even if there is no work to perform.

kanz.f: Is an Exclusive Employee liable for items destroyed in their possession while performing their duties?
kanz.b: No, they are generally not liable.

kanz.f: What are some of the primary reasons that terminate a lease contract?
kanz.b: Defects, ruin of the property, loss of water for mills, or the death of either party (if the lease was for themselves).

kanz.f: What is a "legal excuse" ('Udhr) in the context of canceling a lease?
kanz.b: The inability of a party to proceed without incurring excessive, unexpected harm.

kanz.f: Can you provide examples of a legitimate "excuse" ('Udhr) for lease annulment?
kanz.b: A merchant becoming bankrupt, a travel plan being canceled, or a dental condition making a procedure unnecessary.

kanz.f: What is the definition of Kitabah?
kanz.b: A contract where a slave gains immediate freedom to work, with ownership of their person transitioning to freedom upon full payment.

kanz.f: What happens to a Mukatab slave if they pay all agreed installments?
kanz.b: They become free.

kanz.f: What happens to a Mukatab slave if they fail to pay the installments?
kanz.b: They revert to slavery.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if a Kitabah contract involves prohibited items (e.g., alcohol, pork)?
kanz.b: The contract is invalid, though the slave may still be freed upon payment, with an obligation to pay the slave's value.

kanz.f: What are some actions a Mukatab is permitted to perform?
kanz.b: Sell, buy, travel, marry their slave, and contract their slave.

kanz.f: To whom does the wala' (patronage) belong if a Mukatab pays their debt after being freed?
kanz.b: To the Mukatab themselves.

kanz.f: Name three actions that a Mukatab is prohibited from performing.
kanz.b: Marrying without permission, giving significant gifts, and guaranteeing debts.

kanz.f: What is the status of the father or child if a Mukatab purchases them?
kanz.b: They also become Mukatab.

kanz.f: Is it valid to enter a Mukatabah contract with an Umm al-Walad or a Mudabbar?
kanz.b: Yes.

kanz.f: What happens to the Mukatabah contract if the master dies?
kanz.b: It is not voided; the slave pays the installments to the master's heirs.

kanz.f: If a Mukatab dies leaving enough wealth to cover the contract, what happens?
kanz.b: The contract is fulfilled, the debt is paid from their estate, and they are declared free just before death.

kanz.f: How is Wala' defined?
kanz.b: The right of inheritance and patronage between a manumitter and the manumitted person.

kanz.f: In the inheritance hierarchy, where does the manumitter rank?
kanz.b: The manumitter is prioritized over dhawu al-arham (distant relatives) but follows the asaba nasabiyah (agnatic blood relatives).

kanz.f: What is Wala' al-Mu'aqadah (Patronage by Contract)?
kanz.b: A contract between a convert to Islam and a patron, where the patron inherits from the convert and pays their blood money ('aqilah).

kanz.f: What condition must be met for Wala' al-Mu'aqadah to be valid?
kanz.b: The convert must have no other heirs.

kanz.f: Can a convert transfer their Wala' al-Mu'aqadah contract to someone else?
kanz.b: Yes, provided the patron has not yet paid blood money for the convert.

kanz.f: How is Ikrah (Coercion) defined?
kanz.b: An action taken by one person against another that removes the element of free will.

kanz.f: What are the conditions for a valid claim of coercion regarding the threat?
kanz.b: The coercer must be capable of carrying out the threat (e.g., death, severe beating, or prolonged imprisonment).

kanz.f: What is the legal status of a contract entered into under coercion?
kanz.b: The victim has the option to uphold or annul the transaction.

kanz.f: What action constitutes ratification of a transaction originally forced by coercion?
kanz.b: Payment or delivery of the item voluntarily after the coercion ceases.

kanz.f: Does coercion make forbidden acts like consuming pork or wine lawful?
kanz.b: No, unless the threat is death or limb amputation.

kanz.f: What is the ruling if a person is coerced into killing an innocent person?
kanz.b: It is not permitted. Both the killer and the coercer are subject to Qisas (retribution).

kanz.f: What is the legal effect of being coerced into divorce or emancipation?
kanz.b: These acts take legal effect regardless of the coercion.

kanz.f: How is Hajr (Interdiction) defined?
kanz.b: Restricting someone from performing legal transactions (tasarruf) due to minority, enslavement, or insanity.

kanz.f: What is the legal status of transactions made by minors, the insane, or slaves without permission?
kanz.b: The transactions are invalid.

kanz.f: Are minors, slaves, or the insane liable if they damage property?
kanz.b: Yes, they are liable for the value of the damaged property.

kanz.f: If a person reaches puberty without mental maturity (sufh), until what age might they be prevented from managing their property?
kanz.b: Until age 25.

kanz.f: What action may a judge take against an insolvent person burdened by debt?
kanz.b: They may be imprisoned so that their assets can be sold to satisfy creditors.

kanz.f: How does a judge settle a debtor's obligations depending on the genus of their assets and debts?
kanz.b: If they are of the same genus, the judge settles the debt directly; if they differ, the property is sold to settle the debt.

kanz.f: What are the signs of puberty for a boy, and when is it confirmed if those do not occur?
kanz.b: Nocturnal emission or impregnation; confirmed at 18 years if not reached.

kanz.f: What are the signs of puberty for a girl, and when is it confirmed if those do not occur?
kanz.b: Menstruation, pregnancy, or nocturnal emission; confirmed at 17 years if not reached.

kanz.f: What is the legal maturity age for both genders, and what are the minimum ages for puberty?
kanz.b: Legal maturity is 15; minimum age is 12 for boys and 9 for girls.

kanz.f: How is a Ma'dhun (Authorized Slave) defined?
kanz.b: A slave to whom the master has granted permission to trade.

kanz.f: What are the scope and limitations of the Ma'dhun's powers?
kanz.b: Permitted to trade/contract debt; prohibited from marrying, manumitting, or gifting (except minor hospitality).

kanz.f: To what are the debts of a Ma'dhun attached?
kanz.b: The debts are attached to the person of the slave.

kanz.f: What events lead to the revocation of the Ma'dhun's authorization?
kanz.b: Master's death, insanity, apostasy, or the slave absconding.

kanz.f: How is Ghasb (Usurpation) defined?
kanz.b: Appropriating someone’s property without a legal right.

kanz.f: What is the primary obligation of a usurper regarding the usurped item?
kanz.b: To return the original item.

kanz.f: What is the liability of a usurper if the usurped item is destroyed?
kanz.b: They must provide an equivalent (mithli) or, if none exists, the value as of the day of usurpation.

kanz.f: What is the liability of a usurper regarding usurped land?
kanz.b: Liability for the diminution in value caused by the usurper's use, but not for the land itself.

kanz.f: If a usurper builds or plants on usurped land, what must they do?
kanz.b: They must remove the structures/plants and return the land, compensating for any damage caused by the removal.

kanz.f: If a usurper improves an item (e.g., dyes fabric), what options does the owner have?
kanz.b: Take the item and compensate for the value added by the work, or leave the item and demand the value of the original materials.

kanz.f: When does ownership of a usurped item transfer to the usurper?
kanz.b: If the item is destroyed and the usurper pays its full value.

kanz.f: Is a Muslim liable for usurping or destroying another Muslim’s wine or pigs?
kanz.b: No, as they have no legal value in Islamic law.

kanz.f: What is the rule if a Muslim usurps or destroys wine or pigs owned by a Dhimmi?
kanz.b: The Muslim is liable for the damages.

kanz.f: What is the liability of a usurper regarding musical instruments or vinegar?
kanz.b: The usurper is liable for damages, even if they destroy them.

kanz.f: How is Shuf'ah (Pre-emption) defined?
kanz.b: The right to acquire property by force from the purchaser at the price it was sold for.

kanz.f: What is the order of priority for those who can claim Shuf'ah?
kanz.b: 1. Co-owner (khalit fi nafs al-mabi'), 2. Partner in easements (khalit fi haqq al-mabi'), 3. Adjacent neighbor (al-jar al-mulasiq).

kanz.f: How is the right of Shuf'ah formally established and finalized?
kanz.b: By declaring the intention (ishhad) and finalized by mutual consent or a judge's ruling.

kanz.f: What is the procedure for the shafi' (claimant) upon learning of a sale?
kanz.b: They must declare their intent in the presence of witnesses at the location of the sale, the property, or the purchaser.

kanz.f: When must the shafi' produce the payment for the property?
kanz.b: Not until after the judge’s ruling.

kanz.f: To what type of property does Shuf'ah (Pre-emption) apply?
kanz.b: Only to immovable property ('aqar) sold for a financial price.

kanz.f: Does Shuf'ah apply to movable goods or buildings sold without land?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: Can Shuf'ah be claimed if the property was transferred as a dowry, lease payment, or settlement?
kanz.b: No.

kanz.f: What are the three primary ways the right of Shuf'ah can be voided?
kanz.b: Failing to act promptly, compromising the right for money, or selling the property upon which the right is based before judgment.

kanz.f: How is Qismah (Partition) defined?
kanz.b: The process of dividing joint ownership into individual, specified shares.

kanz.f: When can a partner compel others to perform a partition?
kanz.b: When the partners own property of the same type.

kanz.f: Why are certain items (e.g., jewelry, baths) prohibited from being partitioned without consent?
kanz.b: Because they cannot be divided without destroying their value.

kanz.f: What is the standard procedure for conducting a partition?
kanz.b: An expert partitioner (qasim) is appointed to measure, value, draw the shares, and cast lots.

kanz.f: What is the consequence of discovering "gross injustice" (ghabn fahish) in a partition?
kanz.b: The partition is annulled.

kanz.f: In the event of eviction (third-party claim), how is the loss handled?
kanz.b: The affected partner claims the value of their loss from the other partner's share rather than annulling the partition.

kanz.f: What is Tahayya' (Rotational Usage) and to which items does it apply?
kanz.b: An agreement to alternate use of property; valid for houses and slaves, but generally not for fruits, milk, or rideable animals.

kanz.f: How is Muzara'ah (Sharecropping) defined?
kanz.b: A contract for cultivation where the yield is shared between the parties.

kanz.f: What are the necessary conditions for a valid Muzara'ah contract?
kanz.b: Must specify the duration, land, seed owner, seed type, and share distribution; input contributions (land, seeds, labor, oxen) must be in a valid combination.

kanz.f: What happens if a sharecropping contract stipulates a fixed amount of yield (e.g., "so many bushels")?
kanz.b: The contract is invalid.

kanz.f: If a Muzara'ah contract is found invalid, what is the entitlement of the worker?
kanz.b: They are entitled to a fair wage (ajr al-mithl) for their labor, while the yield belongs to the seed owner.

kanz.f: How are post-harvest expenses (harvesting, threshing, winnowing) handled?
kanz.b: They must be shared proportionally; if placed solely on the worker, the contract is invalid.

kanz.f: How is Musaqah (Watering/Gardening) defined?
kanz.b: A contract to maintain trees (orchards, vines) for a share of the produced fruit.

kanz.f: Under what conditions is a Musaqah contract valid?
kanz.b: It is valid if the trees already bear fruit and the worker's labor effectively increases the yield.

kanz.f: What events lead to the termination of a Musaqah contract?
kanz.b: The death of either party or a legitimate legal excuse (such as the worker's illness).

kanz.f: Who is qualified to perform valid Dhaba'ih (slaughtering)?
kanz.b: A Muslim or a Kitabi (Person of the Scripture).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on mentioning the name of Allah during slaughter?
kanz.b: It is mandatory; intentional omission invalidates the slaughter, but accidental omission is forgiven.

kanz.f: What is the required method for a valid slaughter?
kanz.b: Cutting the windpipe, esophagus, and the two jugular veins (cutting any three of these four is sufficient).

kanz.f: What are the requirements for the tool used in slaughtering?
kanz.b: It must be sharp and capable of causing rapid blood flow.

kanz.f: Which types of animals are prohibited for consumption?
kanz.b: Carnivorous animals with fangs, birds of prey with talons, common crows, hyenas, lizards, turtles, insects, domestic donkeys, mules, and horses.

kanz.f: What animals are explicitly mentioned as permissible to consume?
kanz.b: Rabbits, locusts, and fish (provided they are not found floating dead).

kanz.f: What is the effect of slaughtering an animal whose meat is forbidden (but not human or swine)?
kanz.b: It purifies the meat and the hide.

kanz.f: For whom is Udhiyah (Sacrifice) considered Wajib?
kanz.b: Every free, Muslim, resident, and wealthy (musir) individual.

kanz.f: Which animals are valid for Udhiyah?
kanz.b: Sheep, goats, cattle, or camels.

kanz.f: What are the requirements for an animal to be valid for Udhiyah?
kanz.b: It must be free of major defects, such as blindness, lameness, or missing ears/tails.

kanz.f: How many people can share a single camel or cow for Udhiyah?
kanz.b: Up to seven people.

kanz.f: What is the requirement regarding the intention of those sharing a cow or camel?
kanz.b: All must intend the sacrifice; if one intends only meat, the sacrifice is invalid for all.

kanz.f: What is the recommended distribution of the Udhiyah?
kanz.b: One-third should be distributed as charity.

kanz.f: What is the proper usage for the hide of the sacrificial animal?
kanz.b: It should be given in charity or used for household items.

kanz.f: How does Imam Muhammad رحمه الله classify Makruh (abominable) acts?
kanz.b: He classifies them as essentially Haram (forbidden).

kanz.f: What is the ruling on using gold or silver vessels for eating, drinking, or perfume?
kanz.b: It is forbidden for both men and women.

kanz.f: Under what condition is it permitted to sit on or drink from a silver-inlaid chair or vessel?
kanz.b: If one avoids touching the silver parts.

kanz.f: What are the restrictions on men wearing silk?
kanz.b: Pure silk is forbidden, though a four-finger width is permissible.

kanz.f: What is the ruling on a man wearing a silver ring?
